When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.

The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
lemma was applied.

The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
prose.

\section{Concision and Readability}

A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.

The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
derivation genuinely needs room.

Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.

If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
the issue or pull request in a footnote.

\section{When the Investigation Starts}

The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
argument.

The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
relevant files already compile.

At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
formalized.

A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
mathematics.

Once a cited statement is established to be mathematically false, the repair
and escalation procedure is governed by Section~6 of
\path{local/protocols/issues-prs.md}.  Before asking the human owner to choose a
replacement, a dedicated mathematical-gap session must produce a correction
which is correct, sufficient for every paper and blueprint use, and minimal,
then iterate it against the Lean statement and its downstream consumers.  A
Claude Fable~5.1 session is currently launched by the owner session through its
Agent tool; a Codex main session requests that lane on progress log~\#27 rather
than dispatching a Codex worker.  Only after the astra poller reports
availability on owner inbox~\#26 does the Codex route become
\texttt{dispatch.sh --role mathfix} with astra.  A change to a mathematical
definition or game is escalated immediately; other repairs reach the owner
inbox only after the shared convergence budget expires.

Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
implementation.

\section{When to Write a Note}

A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
relation.

A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.

Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.

When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
though it were the paper theorem.

This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
argument.

A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.

\section{Counterexamples}

If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.

When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.

\section{Revision of a Note}

A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
which point remains unsettled.

Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
discussion.

\section{Form of the Note}

Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant
source article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the
original passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may
be linked with \verb|\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be
recorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should
serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized
around the mathematical assertion and its proof.

The note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for
measurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters
should be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the
state should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can
be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.

Only the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar
substitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote
a long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or
proposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or
logical implication in which the discrepancy appears.

Displayed equations should be used with restraint.  They are appropriate for the
source estimate being checked, the cited estimate in the form actually used, and
the calculation where a term or hypothesis appears or disappears.  When a
displayed equation is identified by a source label, the label should appear on
the right of the display, while the surrounding prose refers to the mathematical
assertion itself.  The standard \texttt{amsmath} command \verb|\tag| is the
right mechanism for this; a separate local convention should be introduced only
if the standard mechanism is genuinely insufficient.  For a multi-line aligned
display, tag the individual lines that carry the source information rather than
forcing a long combined label below the equations.  Short
scalar definitions and elementary inequalities should remain inline when the
sentence reads better that way.  As in ordinary mathematical writing, a displayed
formula is part of the surrounding sentence and should be punctuated accordingly.

Bibliographic entries used only by these notes should live in
\path{docs/paper-gaps/references.bib}.  A new note should ordinarily begin from
\path{docs/paper-gaps/template.tex}, which records the common LaTeX preamble,
the local bibliography, and a model for right-hand source labels in displayed
equations.

Blueprint prose cites a note like any other source, with
\verb|\cite{gap:<slug>}|; the bibliography entry in
\path{blueprint/src/references.bib} carries the published URL of the note,
whether the note lives in this repository or in another one.  Lean docstrings
and comments use the repository path form \path{docs/paper-gaps/<slug>.tex}.

The note should then compare the cited source with the informal blueprint, if
there is one, and with the formal statement.  This comparison should be written
in ordinary mathematical prose.  Formal declaration names and source paths should
be supplied only to identify the exact formal statements, and normally belong in
footnotes.

The conclusion should give a verdict.  It may say that there is no discrepancy,
that the matter is only notational, that an intermediate estimate needs a
harmless correction, that a hypothesis is missing, that there is a theorem-level
gap, or that the question remains open.  The classification should reflect the
mathematics, not the amount of formal work required.

  1422	\[ \hat{S}^X_g = \sum_{g_\zpt} \hat{S}_{g,g_\zpt} \quad  \text{and}  \quad \hat{S}^Z_g = \sum_{g_\xpt} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g}\;,\]

  1426	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tauwu}

   453		For the first item, the self-consistency of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ (Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}) is equivalent, since these observables are Hermitian involutions (Lemma~\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}), to $\E_{j \in \{0,\ldots,t-1\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M} \bra{\hat\psi} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ot \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat\psi} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$; setting $\ket{\vartheta} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$ and using the exact conjugation identities of Lemma~\ref{lem:v-swap-conjugation}, this becomes $\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$, where $H_W = \E_j \E_{\tilde{u}} \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \bigl( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \ot \tau^W(s) \bigr)^{\ot M}$ by the tensor factorization of $\tau^W(\tilde{u})$ and the invariance of the uniform average over $s$ under $s \mapsto e_j s$.    455		% without ensuring that it is nonzero; see Remark rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip.
   456		If $\delta_P > 1/8$, then, after enlarging the universal constant in $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, both items of the lemma hold with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ an arbitrary unit state, since their left-hand sides never exceed $4$; assume therefore $\delta_P \leq 1/8$.    703		documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_extraction-transfer}.

    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.

    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.

    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.

   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,

     ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
       ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
         0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
           ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
             (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)

               (fun u => S.placeSide .alice (tildeObs w .alice W u j))
               (fun u => S.placeSide .bob (tildeObs w .bob W u j))
               S.psiHat ≤
                 deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q := by
   have hcard : 0 ≤ (Fintype.card PauliEdge : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg _
   refine ⟨48 + 32 * (Fintype.card PauliEdge : ℝ), by linarith, ?_⟩
   intro P epsilon deltaG hepsilon hepsilon_one hdeltaG S w W j
   have hbound := (tildeObs_opDistSq_le_pulling_eval_add w W j).trans
     (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
       (add_le_add (pullingMeas_eval_consistencyDefect_le w W) (le_refl _))
       (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 4))
   have heps : epsilon ≤ Real.sqrt epsilon := Real.le_sqrt_self_iff.mpr hepsilon_one
   have hsqrt := Real.sqrt_nonneg epsilon
   have hratio : 0 ≤ (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q :=
     div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) (Nat.cast_nonneg _)) (Nat.cast_nonneg _)
   have hscaled := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left heps
     (mul_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 32) hcard)
   refine hbound.trans ?_
   unfold deltaConstructPaulis
   rw [Nat.cast_mul]
   nlinarith [mul_nonneg hcard hdeltaG, mul_nonneg hcard hratio]

 % In the source the following properties are stated inline with the

 \begin{lemma}[Product form and Pauli relations of the pulled-apart observables]\label{lem:tildew-product-form}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.tildeObs_eq_heteroKron}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.tildeObs_isHermitian}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.tildeObs_mul_self}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.tildeObs_twisted_commutation}
 	\leanok
 	\uses{def:tilde-w-observables, def:s-w-marginals, def:generalized-pauli, def:qld-full-field-decoder, lem:qld-4-7}
 	Let $\tau^W(\cdot)$ denote the generalized Pauli $W$ observable (Definition~\ref{def:generalized-pauli}). For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M$, and $j \in \{0,\ldots,t-1\}$,
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:tildewj-product-form}
 		\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})
 		= \Big( \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \, \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z} \Big) \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})\;,
 	\end{equation}
 	where $g_W$ denotes $g_X$ if $W = X$ and $g_Z$ if $W = Z$. In particular each $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ is Hermitian and squares to the identity. Moreover, the pulled-apart observables satisfy exactly the twisted commutation relations of the generalized Pauli observables $\tau^X(e_j \tilde{u})$ and $\tau^Z(e_{j'} \tilde{v})$: for all $j,j' \in \{0,\ldots,t-1\}$ and $\tilde{u},\tilde{v} \in \F_q^M$,
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:tildew-twisted-commutation}
 		\tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u})\, \tilde{Z}^{j'}(\tilde{v})
 		= (-1)^{\tr((e_j \tilde{u}) \cdot (e_{j'} \tilde{v}))}\, \tilde{Z}^{j'}(\tilde{v})\, \tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u})\;,
 	\end{equation}
 	where $\tr((e_j \tilde{u}) \cdot (e_{j'} \tilde{v})) = \tr(e_j e_{j'} (\tilde{u} \cdot \tilde{v}))$.
 \end{lemma}
 \begin{proof}
 	\leanok
 	\uses{def:tilde-w-observables, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:tau-dot-product-projector, def:s-w-marginals, lem:pauli-observable-expansion, lem:twisted-commutation, lem:qld-4-7}
 	Expanding $\tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \sum_{h} (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\tilde{u} \cdot h))}\, \tau^W_h$ on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:tildewj-product-form} (Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-observable-expansion}), grouping the $h$ according to the value $a' = h \cdot \tilde{u}$ into the projectors $\tau^W_{a'}(\tilde{u})$ of \eqref{eq:def-tauwu}, collecting the pairs $(g_X,g_Z)$ with a common value $g_W = g$ into $\hat{S}^W_g$ (Definition~\ref{def:s-w-marginals}), and changing the summation variable to $a = (\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a'$ recovers, by \eqref{eq:tilde_M} and \eqref{eq:def-tildewj}, the operator $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$; this proves \eqref{eq:tildewj-product-form}. Since the $\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$ are mutually orthogonal projectors summing to the identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}) and $\tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})$ is a Hermitian involution, the product form exhibits $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ as Hermitian with square $\sum_{g_X,g_Z} \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z} \ot \Id = \Id$. For \eqref{eq:tildew-twisted-commutation}, the two sign-weighted sums of the projectors $\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$ appearing in the product forms of $\tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u})$ and $\tilde{Z}^{j'}(\tilde{v})$ commute with each other, so the commutation phase is that of $\tau^X(e_j \tilde{u})$ and $\tau^Z(e_{j'} \tilde{v})$, which is $(-1)^{\tr((e_j \tilde{u}) \cdot (e_{j'} \tilde{v}))}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation}.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{remark}[The commutation phase across basis indices]\label{rem:qld-cross-phase}
 	For $j \neq j'$ the source asserts that $\tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u})$ and $\tilde{Z}^{j'}(\tilde{v})$ commute for all $\tilde{u}, \tilde{v} \in \F_q^M$. By self-duality of the basis $\{e_j\}$, the dichotomy asserted by the source --- commutation for $j \neq j'$, and the phase $(-1)^{\tr((e_j\tilde{u}) \cdot (e_j\tilde{v}))}$ for $j = j'$ --- agrees with \eqref{eq:tildew-twisted-commutation} whenever $\tilde{u} \cdot \tilde{v} \in \{0,1\}$, in particular for all $\tilde{u}, \tilde{v} \in \{0,1\}^M$. The relations \eqref{eq:tildew-twisted-commutation} are not used in the remainder of the chapter.
 	The counterexample and corrected phase are documented in
 	\cite{gap:qpbt_cross-basis-phase}.
 \end{remark}
 
 \section{Consistency with the points measurements}
 
 The next lemma shows that the pulled-apart measurements are consistent with the original points measurements of the strategy, and self-consistent. Write $\delta_G$ for the error of the global polynomial-pair witness supplied by Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}. Assume $0\leq\eps\leq1$ and $\delta_G\geq0$, and put
 \[
 	B = \delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + \frac{md}{q}.
 \]
 Each displayed construction estimate below has its own universal constant $C_E \geq 1$, quantified independently, and its own scale $\delta_P^E=C_EB$. The source uses one enlarged error $\delta_S$ for all of these estimates. The two presentations agree: after the finitely many estimates have been established, take $C_* = \max_E C_E$ and $\delta_P=C_*B$. Since $B\geq0$, every bound remains valid at this common scale. In the proof paragraphs, $\delta_P$ denotes this common enlargement. It has the same asymptotic form as $\delta_G$: after shrinking $b$ to at most $1/2$, the term $\eps^b$ dominates $\sqrt{\eps}$ for $0 \leq \eps \leq 1$, while $(md)^a q^{-b}$ dominates $md/q$.

 \begin{lemma}[The marginals absorb the point measurements]\label{lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_marginalPoly_pointMeas_approx_id}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.marginalPoly_sub_pointMeas_approx_zero}
 	\leanok

 	For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$,
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-sg-cons}
 		\sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot (\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{g(u)})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}''} \approx_{\delta_P^{\mathrm{id}}} \Id
 	\end{equation}
 	and
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-sg-cons2}
 		\bigl(\hat{S}^W_g \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)})\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \approx_{\delta_P^{\mathrm{ann}}} 0\;,
 	\end{equation}
 	where the answer summation is over $g \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$. The independently quantified scale $\delta_P^{\mathrm{ann}}$ includes the additional point-measurement error in \eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons2}. Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations also hold (Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}).
 \end{lemma}
 \begin{proof}
 	\uses{lem:qld-4-7, fact:agreement, fact:add-a-proj, def:bracket, lem:qld-comm-cons}
 	The point-consistency conclusion of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} states that, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
 	\[
 		\bra{\hat\psi} \sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot (\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}''} \ket{\hat\psi} \geq 1 - \delta_G\;,
 	\]
 	which says exactly that the operator on the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons} is $\delta_G$-consistent with $\Id$; Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} and the universal-factor enlargement give the $\approx_{\delta_P}$ statement \eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons}. For \eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons2}, the same consistency, written with the coarse-graining $\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} = \sum_{g : g(u) = a} \hat{S}^W_g$ as $(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \approx_{O(\delta_G)} (\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}''}$ with answer summation over $a \in \F_q$, is left-multiplied by $(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'}$ using Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}; moving $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_a$ from registers $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}''$ to $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'$ costs a further $\eps$ by Cauchy--Schwarz together with the self-consistency of the $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_a$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons}), giving
 	\[
 		(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \approx_{O(\delta_G + \eps)} (\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'}\;.
 	\]
 	Expanding
 	\[
 		\E_u \sum_g \bigl\| (\hat{S}^W_{g} \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)}))_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ket{\hat\psi} \bigr\|^2
 		= \E_u \sum_a \bra{\hat\psi} \bigl((\Id - \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a}) \cdot \hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ket{\hat\psi}
 	\]
 	and bounding the right-hand side by $O(\delta_G + \eps)$ using the two approximations above yields \eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons2} at scale $\delta_P$. The symmetric equivalents follow by the same argument with the register bipartitions interchanged.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{definition}[The swap unitaries]\label{def:v-swap-unitary}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary}
 	\leanok
 	\uses{lem:qld-4-7, def:generalized-pauli, def:qld-full-field-decoder}
 	Define the linear map
 	\[
 		V_{\mathrm{A}} = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \bigl(\tau^X(\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \, \tau^Z(\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}''}\;,
 	\]
 	where $\tau^X(\cdot)$ and $\tau^Z(\cdot)$ are the generalized Pauli observables acting on $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$; note that the argument of $\tau^X$ is $\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\tau^Z$ is $\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)$.  % In the source the following properties are established inline with the
 % definition of the swap unitaries; they are recorded here as a lemma.
 \begin{lemma}[Unitarity and conjugation action of the swap unitaries]\label{lem:v-swap-conjugation}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.conjTranspose_mul_swapUnitary}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_conj_tildeObs}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_conj_tildeM}
 	\leanok
 	\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, def:tilde-w-observables, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:generalized-pauli, def:indicator-vector, def:bracket}
 	The maps $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{B}}$ of Definition~\ref{def:v-swap-unitary} are unitaries acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$ respectively, and their conjugation action is exact, as follows. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $j \in \{0,\ldots,t-1\}$, and $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M$,
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}
 		V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \bigl( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \bigr)_{\mathrm{A}''}
 		\qquad \text{and} \qquad
 		V_{\mathrm{B}} \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot \bigl( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \bigr)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
 	\end{equation}
 	and for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^m$, and $a \in \F_q$,
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
 		V_{\mathrm{B}} \, \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \, V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
 		\qquad
 		\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h \,:\, g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_h\;,
 	\end{equation}
 	together with the analogous identity for $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$.
 \end{lemma}
 \begin{proof}
 	\uses{lem:qld-4-7, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:twisted-commutation, def:v-swap-unitary, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:tau-dot-product-projector, def:indicator-vector, def:decoding-map, def:generalized-pauli}
 	Since the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ is projective (Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}) and the $\tau^X, \tau^Z$ observables are self-inverse,
 	\[
 		V_{\mathrm{A}} V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \Id_{\mathrm{A}''} = \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}\;,
 	\]
 	and the same computation gives $V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger V_{\mathrm{A}} = \Id$, so $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ is unitary; likewise $V_{\mathrm{B}}$. For \eqref{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}, conjugate the product form \eqref{eq:tildewj-product-form} of $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}): by the orthogonality of the projectors $\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$, only the diagonal terms survive, and the twisted commutation relation (Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation})
 	\[
 		\tau^X(\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \, \tau^Z(\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)) \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \, \tau^X(\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \, \tau^Z(\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))
 	\]
 	cancels the sign $(-1)^{\tr(e_j (\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))}$ term by term, leaving $\sum_{g_X,g_Z} \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z} \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \Id \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})$. For \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, expand $\tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$ by \eqref{eq:tilde_M} and \eqref{eq:def-tauwu}; by the orthogonality of the $\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$, conjugation replaces, in the term of $\hat{S}^W_g$, each projector $\tau^W_h$ by $\tau^W_{h + \mathrm{Dec}(g)}$, using the identities $\tau^X(s)\, \tau^Z_h \,\tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h+s}$ and $\tau^Z(s)\, \tau^X_h\, \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h+s}$. Substituting $h' = h + \mathrm{Dec}(g)$ turns the constraint $h \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = (\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)) - a$ into $h' \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = -a = a$, since $\F_q$ has characteristic $2$; the quantity $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ cancels exactly, so no relation between it and $g(u)$ is used (Remark~\ref{rem:qld-decoding-identity}). Since $h' \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g_{h'}(u)$ \eqref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}, summing over $g$ gives \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}; the computation for $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ is identical.
 \end{proof}

 \begin{remark}[Two steps in the source proof of the extraction lemma]\label{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}
 	In the source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, the triangle inequality gives $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq \| (\Id - H_X)\ket{\vartheta} \| + \| (\Id - H_Z)\ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$, so that $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq 4\delta_P$; the source instead asserts the bound $2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ for the \emph{squared} norm, which holds only when $\sqrt{\delta_P} \leq 1/2$, and consequently carries the term $\sqrt{\delta_P}$ into an overlap bound of $1 - 2\delta_P - \sqrt{\delta_P}$. The proof above uses the corrected bound $4\delta_P$, which gives the overlap bound $1 - 4\delta_P$ and leaves the final bound $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}} = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ unchanged. The source proof also normalizes the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ without ensuring that it is nonzero; the case distinction on $\delta_P$ in the proof above supplies this, the conclusions of the lemma being trivial when $\delta_P$ exceeds a universal constant.
 	The numerical corrections and their role in the extraction argument are
 	documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_extraction-transfer}.
 \end{remark}

    60	    let B := rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := J) (pauliRegisterMeas (params := P) W)
    61	    (∑ h : PauliRegister P, ‖applyOperatorToState
    62	      (heteroKron (A.effect h - heteroKron (1 : Op I) (pauliProj W h))
    63	        (1 : Op (J × PauliRegister P))) ideal‖ ^ 2) ≤
    64	      2 * (1 - avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
    65	        ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm theta
    66	          (heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)
    67	            ((B.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)))) +
    68	        2 * ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) + 4 * ‖theta - ideal‖ := by
    69	  dsimp only
    70	  let ideal := reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))

    73	    rw [reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq, haux, eprState_norm, one_mul]
    74	  have hdist := point_distance_le_two_defect
    75	    (leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := J × PauliRegister P) A)
    76	    (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := I × PauliRegister P) B) ideal
    77	  rw [point_defect_eq, hideal, one_pow] at hdist

    79	      applyOperatorToState
    80	          (heteroKron (A.effect h - heteroKron (1 : Op I) (pauliProj W h))

    82	        applyOperatorToState

    99	/-- At construction error at most one, a universal extraction coefficient of
   100	at least eighteen absorbs both the proved state error and the Pauli comparison
   101	error. The collision term and fourth-root scale are exactly those of
   102	`deltaExtract`; there is no parameter-dependent enlargement of the constant. -/
   103	theorem extraction_small_error_absorption (C delta : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ)
   104	    (hC : 18 ≤ C) (hdelta : 0 ≤ delta) (hdelta_one : delta ≤ 1) :
   105	    16 * delta ≤ deltaExtract C delta m d q ∧
   106	      2 * delta + 2 * (((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) + 16 * Real.sqrt delta ≤
   107	        deltaExtract C delta m d q := by
   108	  have hroot := Real.self_le_rpow_of_le_one hdelta hdelta_one
   109	    (by norm_num : (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ 1)
   110	  have hsqrt : Real.sqrt delta ≤ delta ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
   111	    rw [Real.sqrt_eq_rpow]
   112	    exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hdelta hdelta_one (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   113	  have hr : 0 ≤ (((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) := by positivity
   114	  have hp := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hC
   115	    (add_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hdelta (1 / 4)) hr)
   116	  constructor
   117	  · exact (show 16 * delta ≤ 18 * (delta ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) +
   118	      ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) by nlinarith).trans hp
   119	  · exact (show 2 * delta + 2 * (((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) + 16 * Real.sqrt delta ≤
   120	      18 * (delta ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / q) by nlinarith).trans hp
   121

     5	/-!
     6	# Transfer of the complete Pauli overlap between states
     7	
     8	A selected sum of effects of a complete measurement is a positive contraction.
     9	Applied to the product measurement, this bounds the complete overlap operator,
    10	independently of the number of answers. Its expectation changes by at most twice
    11	the distance between unit vectors. Schwartz--Zippel then removes unequal Pauli
    12	encodings after the change of state.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	Blueprint `lem:qld-unitary`; paper
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1827-1858`.
    18	-/

    29	/-- Any selected sum of effects of a complete measurement is a contraction.
    30	The estimate applies to the whole sum and has no outcome-cardinality factor. -/
    31	theorem norm_apply_measurement_sum_le {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
    32	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Measurement α ι) (s : Finset α)
    33	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    34	    ‖applyOperatorToState (∑ a ∈ s, M.effect a) psi‖ ≤ ‖psi‖ := by
    35	  have hpos : 0 ≤ ∑ a ∈ s, M.effect a := Finset.sum_nonneg (fun a _ => M.pos a)
    36	  have hle : ∑ a ∈ s, M.effect a ≤ 1 := by
    37	    rw [← M.sum_eq_one]
    38	    exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ s)
    39	      (fun a _ _ => M.pos a)
    40	  apply MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_le
    41	  rw [(Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hpos).isHermitian.eq]
    42	  exact (MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self hpos hle).trans hle
    43	
    44	/-- Changing a unit vector changes the expectation of a contraction by at most
    45	twice the vector distance. No positivity or self-adjointness is required. -/
    46	theorem abs_stateQForm_sub_le_of_contraction {ι : Type*}
    47	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (T : Op ι)
    48	    (hT : ∀ v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι, ‖applyOperatorToState T v‖ ≤ ‖v‖)
    49	    (psi phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hpsi : ‖psi‖ = 1) (hphi : ‖phi‖ = 1) :
    50	    |stateQForm psi T - stateQForm phi T| ≤ 2 * ‖psi - phi‖ := by
    51	  have hsplit : stateQForm psi T - stateQForm phi T =
    52	      (inner ℂ (psi - phi) (applyOperatorToState T psi)).re +
    53	        (inner ℂ phi (applyOperatorToState T (psi - phi))).re := by
    54	    simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]
    55	  rw [hsplit]
    56	  calc
    57	    _ ≤ |(inner ℂ (psi - phi) (applyOperatorToState T psi)).re| +
    58	        |(inner ℂ phi (applyOperatorToState T (psi - phi))).re| := abs_add_le _ _
    59	    _ ≤ ‖psi - phi‖ * ‖applyOperatorToState T psi‖ +
    60	        ‖phi‖ * ‖applyOperatorToState T (psi - phi)‖ :=
    61	      add_le_add ((Complex.abs_re_le_norm _).trans (norm_inner_le_norm _ _))
    62	        ((Complex.abs_re_le_norm _).trans (norm_inner_le_norm _ _))
    63	    _ ≤ ‖psi - phi‖ * ‖psi‖ + ‖phi‖ * ‖psi - phi‖ :=
    64	      add_le_add (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hT psi) (norm_nonneg _))
    65	        (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hT (psi - phi)) (norm_nonneg _))
    66	    _ = _ := by rw [hpsi, hphi]; ring
    67	
    68	/-- The complete diagonal overlap of two local measurements is stable under a
    69	change of unit state. The tensor factors can have different dimensions. -/
    70	theorem abs_diagonal_overlap_state_sub_le {α I J : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    72	    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] (A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement α J)
    73	    (psi phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (hpsi : ‖psi‖ = 1) (hphi : ‖phi‖ = 1) :
    74	    |(∑ a, stateQForm psi (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a))) -
    75	      ∑ a, stateQForm phi (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a))| ≤
    76	        2 * ‖psi - phi‖ := by
    77	  let s := Finset.univ.filter (fun ab : α × α => ab.1 = ab.2)
    78	  have heq : (∑ ab ∈ s, (tensorMeasurement A B).effect ab) =
    79	      ∑ a, heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a) := by
    80	    simp [s, Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type, tensorMeasurement,
    81	      Measurement.ofSumEqOne]
    82	  have h := abs_stateQForm_sub_le_of_contraction _
    83	    (norm_apply_measurement_sum_le (tensorMeasurement A B) s) psi phi hpsi hphi
    84	  rw [heq, stateQForm_finset_sum, stateQForm_finset_sum] at h
    85	  exact h

    87	/-- Averaging evaluated overlaps does not increase the state-transfer cost.
    88	This controls the complete overlap in paper `eq:qld-unitary-9`. -/
    89	theorem evaluated_overlap_state_transfer {Y α R I J : Type*}
    90	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    91	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    92	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    93	    (A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement α J) (eval : α → Y → R)
    94	    (psi phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (hpsi : ‖psi‖ = 1) (hphi : ‖phi‖ = 1) :
    95	    avgOver (uniformDistribution Y) (fun y => ∑ r, stateQForm psi
    96	      (heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)).effect r)
    97	        ((B.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)).effect r))) ≤
    98	      avgOver (uniformDistribution Y) (fun y => ∑ r, stateQForm phi
    99	        (heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)).effect r)
   100	          ((B.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)).effect r))) + 2 * ‖psi - phi‖ := by
   101	  have h := avgOver_mono (uniformDistribution Y) _ _ (fun y =>
   102	    (le_abs_self _).trans (abs_diagonal_overlap_state_sub_le
   103	      (A.postprocess (fun a => eval a y)) (B.postprocess (fun a => eval a y))
   104	      psi phi hpsi hphi))
   105	  rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability _
   106	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)] at h
   107	  linarith

   109	/-- Two distinct Pauli answers have encodings agreeing on at most an `md/q`
   110	fraction of points. Injectivity follows from the exact decoder identity. -/
   111	theorem pauli_encoding_collision_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
   112	    (h k : PauliRegister P) (hne : h ≠ k) :
   113	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   114	      (fun u => if evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u = evalPoly (encodingPoly k) u
   115	        then (1 : ℝ) else 0) ≤ (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q := by
   116	  apply poly_eval_collision_le
   117	  intro heq
   118	  apply hne
   119	  have hd := congrArg (fun g : Poly P => decodeFq g) heq
   120	  simpa only [decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding] using hd
   121	
   122	/-- The unevaluated Pauli overlap on a unit comparison state is bounded below
   123	by the evaluated overlap on another unit state, minus the collision and state
   124	errors. This combines paper `eq:qld-unitary-8` with the transfer following
   125	`eq:qld-unitary-9`, without any dimension or answer-count factor. -/
   126	theorem pauli_overlap_transfer {P : AdmissibleParams} {I J : Type*}
   127	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   128	    (A : Measurement (PauliRegister P) I) (B : Measurement (PauliRegister P) J)
   129	    (theta ideal : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
   130	    (htheta : ‖theta‖ = 1) (hideal : ‖ideal‖ = 1) :
   131	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
   132	      ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm theta
   133	        (heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)
   134	          ((B.postprocess (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a))) ≤
   135	      (∑ h, stateQForm ideal (heteroKron (A.effect h) (B.effect h))) +
   136	        (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q + 2 * ‖theta - ideal‖ := by
   137	  have ht := evaluated_overlap_state_transfer A B
   138	    (fun h u => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u) theta ideal htheta hideal
   139	  have hc := SandwichProduct.avg_diagonal_postprocess_stateQForm_le A B ideal
   140	    (fun h u => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u) ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) hideal
   141	    (by positivity) pauli_encoding_collision_le
   142	  exact ht.trans (add_le_add hc le_rfl)
   143

    28	/-- Simultaneous unitary conjugation preserves the quadratic form of a product. -/
    29	theorem stateQForm_conjBy_mul_apply {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    30	    (U A B : Op I) (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ I) :
    31	    stateQForm (applyOperatorToState U psi) (conjBy U A * conjBy U B) =
    32	      stateQForm psi (A * B) := by
    33	  rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul]
    34	  congr 1
    35	  simp only [conjBy]
    36	  calc
    37	    _ = (Uᴴ * U) * A * (Uᴴ * U) * B * (Uᴴ * U) := by noncomm_ring
    38	    _ = A * B := by rw [hU]; simp

    49	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne

    51	    (fun h => by
    52	      apply star_right_conjugate_nonneg
    53	      exact kronecker_nonneg
    54	        (kronecker_nonneg ((S.pauliMeas side W).pos h) Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
    55	        Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
    56	    (by
    57	      simp only [conjBy, onPlayer, ← Finset.sum_mul, ← Matrix.mul_sum,
    58	        ← heteroKron_finset_sum_left, (S.pauliMeas side W).sum_eq_one,
    59	        heteroKron_one_one, Matrix.mul_one, swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose])

   147	/-- Multiplying the two block placements is their tensor product in block coordinates. -/

   151	    reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   152	      (heteroKron A B) = S.placeSide .alice A * S.placeSide .bob B := by
   153	  simp only [placeSide, ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   154	    Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.one_mul]
   155	
   156	/-- On the jointly swapped state, the overlap of conjugated block measurements
   157	is one minus their original consistency defect. This is simultaneous unitary
   158	invariance with the exact six-register reassociation. -/
   159	theorem swapped_block_overlap_eq (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
   160	    {X α : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   161	    (mu : Distribution X) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
   162	    (A : X → Measurement α (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   163	    (B : X → Measurement α (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   164	    avgOver mu (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm
   165	      (reindexState (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   166	        (S.applyBoth (swapUnitary w .alice) (swapUnitary w .bob) S.psiHat))
   167	      (heteroKron (conjBy (swapUnitary w .alice) ((A x).effect a))
   168	        (conjBy (swapUnitary w .bob) ((B x).effect a)))) =
   169	      1 - consistencyDefect mu
   170	        (fun x a => S.placeSide .alice ((A x).effect a))
   171	        (fun x a => S.placeSide .bob ((B x).effect a)) S.psiHat := by
   172	  have h := consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap mu
   173	    (fun x => S.blockMeasurement .alice (A x))
   174	    (fun x => S.blockMeasurement .bob (B x)) S.psiHat hmu S.psiHat_norm
   175	  simp only [blockMeasurement_effect] at h
   176	  rw [h, sub_sub_cancel]
   177	  apply avgOver_congr
   178	  intro x
   179	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   180	  intro a _
   181	  rw [WinImplications.stateQForm_reindexState, S.reindexOp_heteroKron_eq_placeSides]
   182	  erw [← S.conjBy_placeBoth_swap_placeSide w .alice,
   183	    ← S.conjBy_placeBoth_swap_placeSide w .bob]
   184	  exact stateQForm_conjBy_mul_apply _ _ _ (S.placeBoth_swap_left_unitary w) S.psiHat
   185	
   186	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   187	/-- Alice's evaluated swapped total-Pauli overlap with Bob's canonical
   188	measurement is exactly one minus the evaluated-Pauli/tilde consistency defect. -/
   189	theorem swapped_pauli_overlap_alice (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) :
   190	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
   191	      ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm
   192	        (reindexState (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   193	          (S.applyBoth (swapUnitary w .alice) (swapUnitary w .bob) S.psiHat))
   194	        (heteroKron (((S.swappedPauliMeas w .alice W).postprocess
   195	          (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)
   196	          (((rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)
   197	            (pauliRegisterMeas (params := P) W)).postprocess
   198	            (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a))) =
   199	      1 - consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   200	        (fun u a => S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pauliEvalMeas .alice W u).effect a))
   201	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a)) S.psiHat := by
   202	  simp only [S.swappedPauliMeas_eval_effect]
   203	  simp_rw [S.canonical_eval_eq_conj_tildeM w .bob]
   204	  have h := S.swapped_block_overlap_eq w _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)
   205	    (fun u => leftPlacedMeasurement (leftPlacedMeasurement (S.pauliEvalMeas .alice W u)))
   206	    (fun u => Measurement.ofSumEqOne (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u))
   207	      (fun a => (tildeM_isProj w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a).nonneg)
   208	      (sum_tildeM_eq_one w .bob W (indicatorVec u)))
   209	  have hplace (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :=
   210	    S.placeSide_onPlayer .alice ((S.pauliEvalMeas .alice W u).effect a)
   211	  convert
   212	    (h.trans (congrArg (fun f => 1 - consistencyDefect _ f _ S.psiHat)
   213	      (funext fun u => funext fun a => hplace u a))) using 1 <;> rfl
   214	
   215	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   216	/-- Bob's evaluated swapped total-Pauli overlap with Alice's canonical
   217	measurement satisfies the same exact transport, without strategy symmetry. -/
   218	theorem swapped_pauli_overlap_bob (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) :
   219	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
   220	      ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm
   221	        (reindexState (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   222	          (S.applyBoth (swapUnitary w .alice) (swapUnitary w .bob) S.psiHat))
   223	        (heteroKron (((rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)
   224	            (pauliRegisterMeas (params := P) W)).postprocess
   225	            (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a)
   226	          (((S.swappedPauliMeas w .bob W).postprocess
   227	            (fun h => evalPoly (encodingPoly h) u)).effect a))) =
   228	      1 - consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   229	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice (tildeM w .alice W (indicatorVec u) a))
   230	        (fun u a => S.placePlayer .bob ((S.pauliEvalMeas .bob W u).effect a)) S.psiHat := by
   231	  simp only [S.swappedPauliMeas_eval_effect]
   232	  simp_rw [S.canonical_eval_eq_conj_tildeM w .alice]
   233	  have h := S.swapped_block_overlap_eq w _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)
   234	    (fun u => Measurement.ofSumEqOne (tildeM w .alice W (indicatorVec u))
   235	      (fun a => (tildeM_isProj w .alice W (indicatorVec u) a).nonneg)
   236	      (sum_tildeM_eq_one w .alice W (indicatorVec u)))
   237	    (fun u => leftPlacedMeasurement (leftPlacedMeasurement (S.pauliEvalMeas .bob W u)))
   238	  have hplace (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :=
   239	    S.placeSide_onPlayer .bob ((S.pauliEvalMeas .bob W u).effect a)
   240	  convert
   241	    (h.trans (congrArg (fun f => 1 - consistencyDefect _ _ f S.psiHat)
   242	      (funext fun u => funext fun a => hplace u a))) using 1 <;> rfl
   243

     3	/-! # Consistency under independent additive convolution
     4	
     5	Adding the outcomes of an independently perfectly correlated ancillary measurement
     6	pair preserves the consistency defect. The four register types are independent;
     7	`prodShuffle` places the two registers of each player next to one another.
     8	
     9	These are formalization-only auxiliary identities. Perfect ancillary correlation
    10	is a hypothesis of the generic result, to be proved for the Pauli measurements
    11	before applying it to the expanded point construction.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-438`,
    16	  the expanded state and the convolution formula for expanded point effects.
    17	- The same paper, `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`.
    18	- Blueprint `def:expanded-state` and `def:expanded-point-measurement`.
    19	- Issue #266; the ideal-point specialization is the separate issue #267.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    27	open MIPStarRE.Quantum DistanceCalculus
    28	
    29	section Factorization
    30	
    31	variable {ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
    32	  [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    33	  [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
    34	
    35	/-- Joint expectations factor after regrouping an independent pair of bipartite
    36	states by player. The shuffle sends `((i, j), (k, l))` to `((i, k), (j, l))`. -/
    37	theorem inner_prodShuffle_vecTensor_heteroKron
    38	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB))
    39	    (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) (R : Op κA) (T : Op κB) :
    40	    inner ℂ (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor ψ φ))
    41	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (heteroKron A R) (heteroKron B T))
    42	          (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor ψ φ))) =
    43	      inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron A B) ψ) *
    44	        inner ℂ φ (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron R T) φ) := by
    45	  simp only [applyOperatorToState, Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply,
    46	    EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]
    47	  simp_rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
    48	  rw [← (prodShuffle : (ιA × ιB) × (κA × κB) ≃ _).sum_comp]
    49	  simp_rw [← (prodShuffle : (ιA × ιB) × (κA × κB) ≃ _).sum_comp]
    50	  change (∑ p : (ιA × ιB) × (κA × κB), ∑ q : (ιA × ιB) × (κA × κB),
    51	    ((A p.1.1 q.1.1 * R p.2.1 q.2.1) * (B p.1.2 q.1.2 * T p.2.2 q.2.2) *
    52	      (ψ q.1 * φ q.2)) * star (ψ p.1 * φ p.2)) =
    53	    ∑ i : ιA × ιB, ∑ j : ιA × ιB, ∑ k : κA × κB, ∑ l : κA × κB,
    54	      ((A i.1 j.1 * B i.2 j.2 * ψ j) * star (ψ i)) *
    55	        ((R k.1 l.1 * T k.2 l.2 * φ l) * star (φ k))
    56	  simp only [Fintype.sum_prod_type (α₁ := ιA × ιB) (α₂ := κA × κB), star_mul]
    57	  conv_lhs =>
    58	    arg 2
    59	    ext i
    60	    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    61	  congr! 4 with i j k l
    62	  ring
    63	
    64	/-- For positive ancillary effects, the real joint expectation factors on the
    65	shuffled tensor state. No normalization or positivity of `A` and `B` is needed. -/
    66	theorem stateQForm_prodShuffle_vecTensor_heteroKron
    67	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB))
    68	    (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) {R : Op κA} {T : Op κB}
    69	    (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hT : 0 ≤ T) :
    70	    stateQForm (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor ψ φ))
    71	        (heteroKron (heteroKron A R) (heteroKron B T)) =
    72	      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron A B) * stateQForm φ (heteroKron R T) := by
    73	  have hnonneg := (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
    74	    (kronecker_nonneg hR hT)).dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg φ.ofLp
    75	  have him : (inner ℂ φ (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron R T) φ)).im = 0 := by
    76	    simpa only [applyOperatorToState, Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply,
    77	      EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, dotProduct_comm, heteroKron] using
    78	      (Complex.nonneg_iff.mp hnonneg).2.symm
    79	  simp only [stateQForm, inner_prodShuffle_vecTensor_heteroKron, Complex.mul_re,
    80	    him, mul_zero, sub_zero]
    81	
    82	end Factorization
    83	
    84	/-- An additive convolution of effect families can be indexed by the ancillary
    85	answer alone. This is the finite-fiber form of the expanded point construction. -/
    86	theorem sum_add_fiber_heteroKron {G ι κ : Type*}
    87	    [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [AddCommGroup G]
    88	    (A : G → Op ι) (R : G → Op κ) (z : G) :
    89	    (∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : G × G => p.1 + p.2 = z),
    90	      heteroKron (A p.1) (R p.2)) =
    91	      ∑ c : G, heteroKron (A (z - c)) (R c) := by
    92	  rw [Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_comm]
    93	  simp only [← eq_sub_iff_add_eq, Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
    94	
    95	/-- Averaging a common additive shift preserves the off-diagonal mass of any
    96	weight function. The ancillary joint weights are supported on the diagonal
    97	and have total diagonal mass one. -/
    98	private theorem sum_convolution_off_diagonal_eq {G : Type*}
    99	    [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [AddCommGroup G]
   100	    (p q : G → G → ℝ) (hzero : ∀ c d, c ≠ d → q c d = 0)
   101	    (hdiag : ∑ c : G, q c c = 1) :
   102	    (∑ z : G, ∑ w : G, if z = w then 0 else
   103	      ∑ c : G, ∑ d : G, p (z - c) (w - d) * q c d) =
   104	      ∑ a : G, ∑ b : G, if a = b then 0 else p a b := by
   105	  have hinner (z w c : G) :
   106	      (∑ d : G, p (z - c) (w - d) * q c d) =
   107	        p (z - c) (w - c) * q c c := by
   108	    apply Finset.sum_eq_single c
   109	    · intro d _ hdc
   110	      rw [hzero c d hdc.symm, mul_zero]
   111	    · simp
   112	  have hshift (c : G) :
   113	      (∑ z : G, ∑ w : G, if z = w then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)) =
   114	        ∑ a : G, ∑ b : G, if a = b then 0 else p a b := by
   115	    refine Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.subRight c) _ _ fun z => ?_
   116	    refine Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.subRight c) _ _ fun w => ?_
   117	    change (if z = w then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)) =
   118	      if z - c = w - c then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)
   119	    simp only [sub_left_inj]
   120	  simp_rw [hinner]
   121	  calc
   122	    (∑ z : G, ∑ w : G, if z = w then 0 else
   123	        ∑ c : G, p (z - c) (w - c) * q c c) =
   124	        ∑ z : G, ∑ w : G, ∑ c : G,
   125	          (if z = w then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)) * q c c := by
   126	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   127	      intro z _
   128	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   129	      intro w _
   130	      by_cases hzw : z = w <;> simp [hzw]
   131	    _ = ∑ c : G, (∑ z : G, ∑ w : G,
   132	        if z = w then 0 else p (z - c) (w - c)) * q c c := by
   133	      simp_rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   134	      conv_lhs =>
   135	        arg 2
   136	        ext z
   137	        rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   138	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   139	    _ = _ := by
   140	      simp_rw [hshift]
   141	      rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hdiag, mul_one]
   142	
   143	/-- Independent additive convolution with a normalized, perfectly correlated
   144	ancillary POVM pair preserves the consistency defect exactly. All four register
   145	types may differ, and neither the original state nor the question distribution
   146	needs to be normalized. No measurement is assumed projective.
   147	
   148	This is a generic auxiliary for the expanded point construction in paper
   149	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-438` and
   150	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, not the latter paper theorem. Its ancillary
   151	perfection hypothesis must be established for the concrete ideal measurements
   152	before specialization; that application is tracked in issue #267. -/
   153	theorem consistencyDefect_convolution_eq_of_perfect
   154	    {X G ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
   155	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [AddCommGroup G]
   156	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   157	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
   158	    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement G ιA) (B : X → Measurement G ιB)
   159	    (R : X → Measurement G κA) (T : X → Measurement G κB)
   160	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB))
   161	    (hφ : ‖φ‖ = 1)
   162	    (hperfect : ∀ x, (∑ c : G, ∑ d : G, if c = d then 0 else
   163	      stateQForm φ (heteroKron ((R x).effect c) ((T x).effect d))) = 0) :
   164	    consistencyDefect μ
   165	        (fun x z => heteroKron
   166	          (∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : G × G => p.1 + p.2 = z),
   167	            heteroKron ((A x).effect p.1) ((R x).effect p.2)) 1)
   168	        (fun x z => heteroKron 1
   169	          (∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : G × G => p.1 + p.2 = z),
   170	            heteroKron ((B x).effect p.1) ((T x).effect p.2)))
   171	        (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor ψ φ)) =
   172	      consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
   173	        (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect b)) ψ := by
   174	  unfold consistencyDefect
   175	  simp_rw [consistency_term_eq_stateQForm, placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   176	  apply avgOver_congr
   177	  intro x
   178	  let q : G → G → ℝ := fun c d =>
   179	    stateQForm φ (heteroKron ((R x).effect c) ((T x).effect d))
   180	  have hnonneg (c d : G) : 0 ≤ q c d :=
   181	    stateQForm_nonneg φ (kronecker_nonneg ((R x).pos c) ((T x).pos d))
   182	  have hoff (c d : G) : 0 ≤ (if c = d then 0 else q c d) := by
   183	    split_ifs
   184	    · exact le_rfl
   185	    · exact hnonneg c d
   186	  have hzero (c d : G) (hcd : c ≠ d) : q c d = 0 := by
   187	    have hrow := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg
   188	      (fun c _ => Finset.sum_nonneg (fun d _ => hoff c d))).mp (hperfect x)
   189	    have hterm := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg
   190	      (fun d _ => hoff c d)).mp (hrow c (Finset.mem_univ c)) d (Finset.mem_univ d)
   191	    simpa only [if_neg hcd] using hterm
   192	  have hdiag : ∑ c : G, q c c = 1 := by
   193	    have h := point_defect_eq (leftPlacedMeasurement (R x))
   194	      (rightPlacedMeasurement (T x)) φ
   195	    simp only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement, Measurement.ofSumEqOne,
   196	      placed_product_stateQForm_eq, hperfect x, hφ, one_pow] at h
   197	    dsimp only [q]
   198	    linarith
   199	  have hfactor (a b c d : G) := stateQForm_prodShuffle_vecTensor_heteroKron ψ φ
   200	    ((A x).effect a) ((B x).effect b) ((R x).pos c) ((T x).pos d)
   201	  simp_rw [sum_add_fiber_heteroKron, heteroKron_finset_sum_left,
   202	    heteroKron_finset_sum_right, stateQForm_finset_sum, hfactor]
   203	  exact sum_convolution_off_diagonal_eq
   204	    (fun a b => stateQForm ψ (heteroKron ((A x).effect a) ((B x).effect b)))
   205	    q hzero hdiag
   206	
   207	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# EPR projection from Pauli disagreement
     5	
     6	Averaging the paired Pauli operators contracts the disagreement norm. The X
     7	and Z averages multiply to the EPR projection, giving the corrected projection
     8	estimate directly in the squared-distance formulation.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	Blueprint `lem:qld-unitary`; paper
    13	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1715-1783`;
    14	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_extraction-transfer.tex`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.LDT DistanceCalculus
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	variable {K I R : Type} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    26	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    27	
    28	/-- The averaged paired Pauli operator has squared displacement at most the
    29	mean squared disagreement between the two players. This is Jensen's inequality
    30	in the projection argument at paper lines 1715-1750. -/
    31	theorem norm_sub_pauliCorrelation_sq_le
    32	    (W : PauliKind) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × ((I → K) × (I → K)))) :
    33	    ‖psi - applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation W)) psi‖ ^ 2 ≤
    34	      opDistSq (uniformDistribution (I → K))
    35	        (fun u => heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) 1))
    36	        (fun u => heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron 1 (tauObservable W u))) psi := by
    37	  classical
    38	  let L (u : I → K) :=
    39	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (1 : Op (I → K)))
    40	  let B (u : I → K) :=
    41	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (1 : Op (I → K)) (tauObservable W u))
    42	  let C (u : I → K) :=
    43	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (tauObservable W u))
    44	  have hL (u : I → K) : (L u)ᴴ * L u = 1 := by
    45	    simp only [L, MagicSquareRigidity.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
    46	      heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, tauObservable_conjTranspose_mul_self,
    47	      heteroKron_one_one]
    48	  have halg (u : I → K) : L u * (L u - B u) = 1 - C u := by
    49	    simp only [L, B, C, Matrix.mul_sub, heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul,
    50	      Matrix.mul_one, tauObservable_sq, heteroKron_one_one]
    51	  have hdist : opDistSq (uniformDistribution (I → K)) (fun _ => 1) C psi =
    52	      opDistSq (uniformDistribution (I → K)) L B psi := by
    53	    unfold opDistSq opFamilyDistSq
    54	    simp only [Fintype.sum_unique]
    55	    apply avgOver_congr
    56	    intro u
    57	    rw [← halg, MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_isometry_mul (hL u)]
    58	  have havg : averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (I → K))
    59	      (fun u => (1 : ℂ) • ((1 : Op (R × ((I → K) × (I → K)))) - C u)) =
    60	      1 - heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation W) := by

   111	does not introduce a factor equal to the number of answers. -/

   113	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
   114	    ∑ h : PauliRegister P,
   115	      (conjBy (S.placeSide side (swapUnitary w side))
   116	        (S.placePlayer side ((S.pauliMeas side W).effect h)))ᴴ *
   117	      conjBy (S.placeSide side (swapUnitary w side))
   118	        (S.placePlayer side ((S.pauliMeas side W).effect h)) = 1 := by
   119	  classical
   120	  let U := S.placeSide side (swapUnitary w side)
   121	  have hU : Uᴴ * U = 1 := S.placeSide_swap_left_unitary w side
   122	  have hU' : U * Uᴴ = 1 := mul_eq_one_comm.mp hU
   123	  have hterm (A : Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   124	      (conjBy U A)ᴴ * conjBy U A = U * (Aᴴ * A) * Uᴴ := by
   125	    simp only [conjBy, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.conjTranspose_conjTranspose]

   127	      _ = U * (Aᴴ * (Uᴴ * U) * A) * Uᴴ := by noncomm_ring

   131	  rw [← Finset.sum_mul, ← Matrix.mul_sum, S.sum_placePlayer_pauli_sq,

   226	          (((pullingMeas w .bob W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a))

   230	    ((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u))

   234	    (leftPlacedMeasurement (S.pointMeas .alice W u))

     6	/-!
     7	# Polynomial outcomes in the pulling argument
     8	
     9	The joint measurement of a polynomial marginal and an ideal Pauli register
    10	returns the difference between the polynomial and the encoding of the register.
    11	Decoding this difference gives exactly the pulled-apart measurement. Polynomial
    12	collision estimates apply to these representatives without an encoding-support
    13	restriction on the original marginal.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	- Blueprint `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, Item 2.
    18	- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1530-1605`,
    19	  `eq:qld-pulling-11`, `eq:qld-pulling-12`, and the following symmetry argument.
    20	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`; only decoder linearity and its
    21	  left-inverse identity are used here.
    22	- Issue #520; these auxiliary results do not assert `eq:qld-pulling-cons`.
    23	- The collision estimate compares unequal difference polynomials under uniform
    24	  evaluation.
    25	-/

    39	/-- The outcome `g - g_h` in `eq:qld-pulling-12` is a bounded polynomial
    40	representative, even when `g` is not in the encoding image. -/
    41	def pullingPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (outcome : Poly P × PauliRegister P) : Poly P :=
    42	  outcome.1 - encodingPoly outcome.2
    43	
    44	/-- Decoder linearity identifies the label in `eq:qld-pulling-12`. This uses
    45	`Dec(g_h) = h`, never the reverse identity on arbitrary polynomials. -/
    46	theorem decodeFq_pullingPoly {P : AdmissibleParams}
    47	    (outcome : Poly P × PauliRegister P) :
    48	    decodeFq (pullingPoly outcome) = decodeFq outcome.1 - outcome.2 := by
    49	  have hsub (g h : Poly P) : decodeFq (g - h) = decodeFq g - decodeFq h := by
    50	    funext y
    51	    simp [decodeOn, decodeAt, evalPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_sub]
    52	  rw [pullingPoly, hsub, decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding]
    53	
    54	/-- Equal difference polynomials give identical scalar labels in the symmetric
    55	expression following `eq:qld-pulling-12`, for every register vector. -/
    56	theorem pulling_label_eq_of_poly_eq {P : AdmissibleParams}
    57	    (first second : Poly P × PauliRegister P)
    58	    (h : pullingPoly first = pullingPoly second) (u : PauliRegister P) :
    59	    dotProduct (decodeFq first.1 - first.2) u =
    60	      dotProduct (decodeFq second.1 - second.2) u := by
    61	  rw [← decodeFq_pullingPoly, ← decodeFq_pullingPoly, h]
    62	
    63	/-- The projective measurement with polynomial outcomes `g - g_h` used to
    64	organize the last step of the pulling argument. Its input witness remains
    65	supplied; no global witness is constructed by this definition. -/

    67	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
    68	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
    69	    Measurement (Poly P) (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
    70	  (tensorMeasurement (w.marginalPoly side W) (pauliRegisterMeas W)).postprocess pullingPoly

    72	/-- The joint effects are tensor products of orthogonal projections, and
    73	postprocessing retains projectivity. -/

    88	theorem pullingMeas_postprocess_effect {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
    89	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
    90	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
    91	    ((pullingMeas w side W).postprocess (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)).effect a =
    92	      tildeM w side W u a := by

   110	/-- The coordinate change to two extraction blocks preserves the consistency
   111	defect, including every off-diagonal outcome and the question distribution. -/
   112	private theorem consistencyDefect_placeSide_eq {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon : ℝ}
   113	    {X A : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A]
   114	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (mu : Distribution X)
   115	    (left : X → A → Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace .alice)))
   116	    (right : X → A → Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace .bob))) :

   122	  unfold consistencyDefect
   123	  apply avgOver_congr
   124	  intro x
   125	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   126	  intro a _
   127	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   128	  intro b _
   129	  by_cases hab : a = b

   132	    rw [stateQForm_reindexState, reindexOp_mul]

   138	private theorem polynomial_decoding_defect_le_evaluated_add {P : AdmissibleParams}
   139	    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]

   141	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (hpsi : ‖psi‖ = 1) :

   143	        (fun u a => heteroKron
   144	          ((A.postprocess (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)).effect a) 1)
   145	        (fun u a => heteroKron 1
   146	          ((B.postprocess (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)).effect a)) psi ≤
   147	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   148	        (fun u a => heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a) 1)

   151	  have hcollision := SandwichProduct.point_codeword_defect_le_avg_evaluated_add

   165	decoding. The field-measurement defect is bounded by the evaluated

   182	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob
   183	          (((pullingMeas w .bob W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a))

     4	/-!
     5	# Point overlaps for the difference-polynomial measurement
     6	
     7	Evaluation of the difference polynomial gives `g(u) - g_h(u)`. Unlike
     8	evaluation after decoding, this formula holds for every polynomial outcome.
     9	The resulting point overlaps are the ones supplied by the global witness.

    15	  especially `eq:qld-pulling-2b` and `eq:qld-pulling-12`.

    17	  the two consistency relations of the supplied global measurement.

    30	/-- Evaluation of the difference measurement is a convolution with the ideal
    31	Pauli point projectors. No encoding hypothesis on `g` is needed. -/
    32	theorem pullingMeas_eval_effect {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
    33	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
    34	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    35	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    36	    ((pullingMeas w side W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a =
    37	      ∑ g : Poly P, heteroKron ((w.marginalPoly side W).effect g)
    38	        (tauDotProj W (indicatorVec u) (evalPoly g u - a)) := by
    39	  rw [pullingMeas, Measurement.postprocess_comp]
    40	  have heval (outcome : Poly P × PauliRegister P) :
    41	      evalPoly (pullingPoly outcome) u =
    42	        evalPoly outcome.1 u - dotProduct outcome.2 (indicatorVec u) := by
    43	    change MvPolynomial.eval u (outcome.1.1 - lowDegreeEncoding outcome.2) = _
    44	    rw [MvPolynomial.eval_sub]
    45	    exact congrArg (evalPoly outcome.1 u - ·) (lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct outcome.2 u)
    46	  simp only [Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter, heval,
    47	    tensorMeasurement, Measurement.ofSumEqOne, pauliRegisterMeas]
    48	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    49	  unfold tauDotProj bracketOp
    50	  simp_rw [heteroKron_finset_sum_right, Finset.sum_filter]
    51	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    52	  intro g _
    53	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    54	  intro h _
    55	  have hlabel : evalPoly g u - dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = a ↔
    56	      dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = evalPoly g u - a := by
    57	    constructor <;> intro heq <;> linear_combination -heq

    66	      (((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a) *
    67	        S.placePlayer .bob ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).effect a)) =
    68	      ∑ g : Poly P, S.place .AA' ((w.marginalPoly .alice W).effect g) *
    69	        S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect (evalPoly g u)) := by
