   182	/-- Both evaluated global marginals are consistent with the opposite
   183	encoding-supported reference. The universal square-root coefficient comes
   184	from the two Pauli-basis checks and point self-consistency; it does not assume
   185	the non-encoding support estimate or the existence of a global witness. -/
   186	theorem global_marginal_encoding_consistency :
   187	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
   188	      0 ≤ epsilon → ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
   189	        (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind),
   190	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   191	          (fun u a => heteroKron (((w.marginalPoly .alice W).postprocess
   192	            (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a) 1)
   193	          (fun u a => heteroKron 1 (((S.encodingPauliMeas .bob W).postprocess
   194	            (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a)) (ExtendedLineGame.pairState S) ≤
   195	        deltaG + C * Real.sqrt epsilon ∧
   196	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   197	          (fun u a => heteroKron (((S.encodingPauliMeas .alice W).postprocess
   198	            (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a) 1)
   199	          (fun u a => heteroKron 1 (((w.marginalPoly .bob W).postprocess
   200	            (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a)) (ExtendedLineGame.pairState S) ≤
   201	        deltaG + C * Real.sqrt epsilon := by
   202	  obtain ⟨C1, hC1, hforward⟩ := win_pauli_basis_cons
   203	  obtain ⟨C2, hC2, hreverse⟩ := WinImplications.win_pauli_basis_cons_interchanged_proof
   204	  let E : ℝ := Fintype.card PauliEdge

   301	/-- A marginal acting on `AA'` has the same mass in the extraction-block
   302	notation and the two-player expanded state. The unused registers carry identities. -/
   303	theorem stateQForm_placeSide_alice_tensor_one {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon : ℝ}
   304	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice))
   305	    (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
   306	    stateQForm S.psiHat (S.placeSide .alice (heteroKron A (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)))) =
   307	      stateQForm (ExtendedLineGame.pairState S) (heteroKron A 1) := by
   308	  have hplace : S.placeSide .alice (heteroKron A (1 : Op (PauliRegister P))) =
   309	      S.place .AA' A := by
   310	    ext row col
   311	    simp only [placeSide, sixRegExtractionEquiv, reindexOp, place, heteroKron,
   312	      Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.one_apply, mul_ite, ite_mul]
   313	    split_ifs <;> simp_all
   314	    rfl
   315	  rw [hplace]
   316	  have h := ExtendedLineGame.stateQForm_pairState_eq_AA'_BA'' S A 1 hA
   317	    Matrix.isHermitian_one
   318	  have hone : S.place .BA'' (1 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) = 1 := by
   319	    convert S.place_one .BA'' using 1
   320	    rfl
   321	  rw [hone, Matrix.mul_one] at h
   322	  exact h.symm

    56	/-- Bob's extraction-block placement preserves finite sums. -/
    57	theorem placeSide_bob_finset_sum (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
    58	    {I : Type*} (s : Finset I) (B : I → Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
    59	    S.placeSide .bob (∑ i ∈ s, B i) = ∑ i ∈ s, S.placeSide .bob (B i) := by
    60	  classical
    61	  change reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    62	    (heteroKron (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA)) (∑ i ∈ s, B i)) = _

    64	  ext row col

    68	/-- The convolution formula with its second outcome solved for. This is the
    69	third line of the overlap calculation in paper lines 1483--1492. -/
    70	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_eq_sum_sub (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
    71	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    72	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    73	    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
    74	      ∑ b : PauliScalar P, heteroKron ((S.pointMeas side W u).effect b)
    75	        (tauDotProj W (indicatorVec u) (a - b)) := by
    76	  classical
    77	  change S.expPointOp side W u a = _
    78	  rw [S.expPointOp_eq_convolution]
    79	  simp only [Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    80	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    81	  intro b _
    82	  have h (c : PauliScalar P) : b + c = a ↔ c = a - b := by
    83	    rw [eq_sub_iff_add_eq, add_comm]
    84	  simp only [h, Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_univ, if_true]

    89	/-- The original/pulled-apart overlap is exactly the expanded-point overlap
    90	at the decoded value. This is the first three lines of the proof of Item 1 in

    92	theorem sum_pointMeas_mul_tildeM_eq_decoded_overlap
    93	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
    94	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)
    95	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    96	    (∑ a : PauliScalar P, S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a) *
    97	      S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a)) =
    98	      ∑ g : Poly P, S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
    99	        S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect
   100	          (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))) := by
   101	  classical
   102	  simp only [tildeM, S.placeSide_bob_finset_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
   103	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   104	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   105	  intro g _
   106	  simp only [S.placePlayer_alice_mul_placeSide_bob_tensor]
   107	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← S.place_finset_sum,
   108	    S.pointMeasExp_effect_eq_sum_sub .alice W u]
   109	  rfl

   111	/-- The pulled-apart consistency defect is one minus the decoded overlap.
   112	This packages completeness with the first three lines of the source's
   113	calculation, still without imposing an encoding restriction. -/
   114	theorem tildeM_consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_decoded_overlap
   115	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
   116	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) :
   117	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   118	      (fun u a => S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a))
   119	      (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a)) S.psiHat =
   120	      1 - avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
   121	        ∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   122	          (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   123	            S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect
   124	              (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))))) := by
   125	  classical
   126	  let point := fun u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P =>
   127	    S.placedMeasurement .AA' (leftPlacedMeasurement (S.pointMeas .alice W u))
   128	  let pulled : (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) → Measurement (PauliScalar P)
   129	      (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := fun u =>
   130	    Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   131	      (fun a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a))
   132	      (fun a => by
   133	        apply ProjectiveSetting.reindexOp_nonneg
   134	        exact kronecker_nonneg Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg
   135	          (tildeM_isProj w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a).nonneg)
   136	      (by
   137	        rw [← S.placeSide_bob_finset_sum, sum_tildeM_eq_one]
   138	        change reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   139	          (heteroKron (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   140	            (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))) = 1
   141	        rw [heteroKron_one_one]
   142	        ext row col
   143	        simp [reindexOp, Matrix.one_apply])
   144	  have h := consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
   145	    (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) point pulled S.psiHat
   146	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) S.psiHat_norm
   147	  change consistencyDefect _ _ _ S.psiHat = 1 - avgOver _ (fun u =>
   148	    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   149	      (S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a) *
   150	        S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a))) at h
   151	  refine h.trans ?_
   152	  congr 1
   153	  apply avgOver_congr
   154	  intro u
   155	  rw [← stateQForm_finset_sum, sum_pointMeas_mul_tildeM_eq_decoded_overlap,
   156	    stateQForm_finset_sum]

   159	/-- Replacing polynomial evaluation by decoded evaluation loses at most the
   160	mass of the non-encoding outcomes. This is the support-restricted replacement
   161	for the fourth line of paper lines 1483--1492. No mass estimate is assumed. -/
   162	theorem marginal_eval_overlap_le_decoded_add_nonencoding
   163	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
   164	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)
   165	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   166	    (∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   167	      (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   168	        S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1)))) ≤
   169	      (∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   170	        (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   171	          S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect
   172	            (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))))) +
   173	      ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g : Poly P => ¬ IsEncoding g),
   174	        stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g)) := by
   175	  classical
   176	  have hpos (g : Poly P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   177	      0 ≤ stateQForm S.psiHat
   178	        (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   179	          S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a)) :=
   180	    stateQForm_nonneg _ (S.place_mul_place_nonneg .BB' .AB'' (by trivial)
   181	      ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).pos g) ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).pos a))
   182	  have hsum (g : Poly P) :
   183	      (∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   184	        (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   185	          S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a))) =
   186	        stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g)) := by
   187	    have hc : (∑ a : PauliScalar P,
   188	        S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a)) = 1 :=
   189	      (S.placedMeasurement .AB'' (S.pointMeasExp .alice W u)).sum_eq_one
   190	    rw [← stateQForm_finset_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum, hc, mul_one]
   191	  rw [Finset.sum_filter, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   192	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   193	  intro g _
   194	  by_cases hg : IsEncoding g
   195	  · simp only [hg, not_true_eq_false, if_false, add_zero]
   196	    rw [decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec hg u]
   197	    rfl
   198	  · simp only [hg, not_false_eq_true, if_true]
   199	    have hle := Finset.single_le_sum (fun a _ => hpos g a)
   200	      (Finset.mem_univ (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1))
   201	    rw [hsum] at hle
   202	    exact hle.trans (le_add_of_nonneg_left (hpos g _))

   463	/-- The swap map built from the global polynomial-pair measurement, with the

   467	noncomputable def swapUnitary {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}

   469	    (side : PlayerSide) : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=

   480	Projectivity and completeness of `w.Smeas side` reduce the product to its

   482	theorem swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose {P : AdmissibleParams}

   506	private theorem swapUnitary_conj_controlled {P : AdmissibleParams}

   530	theorem swapUnitary_conj_tildeObs {P : AdmissibleParams}

   547	        tauObservable W (P.model.basis j • u) := by
   548	    rw [conjBy, Matrix.mul_smul, Matrix.smul_mul]

   567	theorem swapUnitary_conj_tildeM {P : AdmissibleParams}
   568	    {epsilon delta : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}

   584	          (dotProduct (decodeFq (W.selectPoly pair)) (indicatorVec u) - a)))]

     4	/-!
     5	# The EPR projection in Pauli extraction
     6	
     7	The product of the averaged, paired X and Z observables is the rank-one
     8	projection onto the EPR vector. This is an algebraic prerequisite for constructing
     9	the auxiliary state in `exists_extractionWitness_ofGlobalPairWitness`.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	Blueprint `lem:qld-unitary`; paper
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1725-1742`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    26	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    27	
    28	/-- The operator `H_W` of the EPR projection argument, averaged over all
    29	generalized Pauli labels. Paper lines 1725-1733 define this average after
    30	reindexing by a nonzero element of the binary basis. -/
    31	def pauliCorrelation (W : PauliKind) : Op ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
    32	  (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
    33	    ∑ u : ι → K, heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (tauObservable W u)
    34	
    35	private theorem avg_phaseSign_dotProduct (v : ι → K) :
    36	    (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
    37	        ∑ u : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct u v)) =
    38	      if v = 0 then 1 else 0 := by
    39	  have h := congrArg (fun A : Op (ι → K) => A v v)
    40	    (pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable .Z (0 : ι → K))
    41	  have hv : pauliProj .Z (0 : ι → K) v v = if v = 0 then 1 else 0 := by
    42	    change (∏ i, if v i = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0) *
    43	      star (∏ i, if v i = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0) = _
    44	    simp only [Fintype.prod_boole, ← funext_iff]
    45	    change (if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0) * star (if v = 0 then 1 else 0) = _
    46	    split <;> simp
    47	  simp only [dotProduct_zero, map_zero, phaseSign, ite_true, one_smul] at h
    48	  rw [hv] at h
    49	  simpa only [Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.sum_apply, smul_eq_mul,
    50	    tauObservable_Z_apply, ite_true, one_mul] using h.symm
    51	
    52	/-- The Z correlation projects onto equal computational-basis labels.
    53	This is the Fourier cancellation in paper lines 1736-1740. -/
    54	theorem pauliCorrelation_Z_apply (x y : (ι → K) × (ι → K)) :
    55	    pauliCorrelation .Z x y = if x = y ∧ y.1 = y.2 then 1 else 0 := by
    56	  simp only [pauliCorrelation, Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.sum_apply, smul_eq_mul,
    57	    heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
    58	  simp_rw [tauObservable_Z_apply]
    59	  by_cases hxy : x = y
    60	  · subst x
    61	    simp only [ite_true, true_and]
    62	    have hphase (u : ι → K) :
    63	        phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct u y.1)) *
    64	            phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct u y.2)) =
    65	          phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct u (y.1 + y.2))) := by
    66	      rw [← phaseSign_add, dotProduct_add, map_add]
    67	    simp_rw [hphase]
    68	    rw [avg_phaseSign_dotProduct]
    69	    letI : CharP K 2 := (Algebra.charP_iff (ZMod 2) K 2).mp (ZMod.charP 2)
    70	    simp only [funext_iff, Pi.add_apply, Pi.zero_apply, CharTwo.add_eq_zero]
    71	  · have h : x.1 ≠ y.1 ∨ x.2 ≠ y.2 := by
    72	      by_contra h
    73	      push Not at h
    74	      exact hxy (Prod.ext h.1 h.2)
    75	    rcases h with h | h <;> simp [h, hxy]
    76	
    77	/-- On a diagonal input, the X correlation is uniform over diagonal outputs.
    78	This is the shift average in paper lines 1739-1742. -/
    79	theorem pauliCorrelation_X_apply_diagonal (x : (ι → K) × (ι → K)) (a : ι → K) :
    80	    pauliCorrelation .X x (a, a) =
    81	      if x.1 = x.2 then (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0 := by
    82	  simp only [pauliCorrelation, Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.sum_apply, smul_eq_mul,
    83	    heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
    84	  simp_rw [tauObservable_X_apply]
    85	  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (x.1 - a)]
    86	  · simp [add_sub_cancel, eq_comm]
    87	  · intro u _ hu
    88	    have h : x.1 ≠ a + u := by
    89	      intro h
    90	      apply hu
    91	      rw [h, add_sub_cancel_left]
    92	    simp [h]
    93	  · simp
    94	
    95	/-- The product `H_X H_Z` is the ordinary rank-one EPR projection, with no
    96	normalized-trace factor. This is the identity at paper lines 1735-1742 used
    97	to construct the auxiliary state in blueprint `lem:qld-unitary`. -/
    98	theorem pauliCorrelation_mul_eq_epr :
    99	    pauliCorrelation (K := K) (ι := ι) .X * pauliCorrelation .Z =
   100	      Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState (ι → K) x)
   101	        (fun y => star (eprState (ι → K) y)) := by
   102	  ext x y
   103	  rw [Matrix.mul_apply]
   104	  simp_rw [pauliCorrelation_Z_apply]
   105	  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single y]
   106	  · by_cases hy : y.1 = y.2
   107	    · rcases y with ⟨a, b⟩
   108	      dsimp only at hy
   109	      subst b
   110	      rw [if_pos ⟨rfl, rfl⟩, mul_one, pauliCorrelation_X_apply_diagonal]
   111	      change (if x.1 = x.2 then (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0) =
   112	        (if x.1 = x.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0) *
   113	          star (if a = a then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
   114	      by_cases hx : x.1 = x.2
   115	      · rw [if_pos hx, if_pos hx, if_pos rfl]
   116	        exact (inv_sqrt_natCast_mul_conj (Fintype.card (ι → K))).symm
   117	      · simp [hx]
   118	    · simp [hy, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply, eprState]
   119	  · intro z _ hz
   120	    simp [hz]
   121	  · simp

   123	/-- Each Pauli correlation average, with an arbitrary auxiliary register,
   124	is a contraction. The triangle inequality
   125	and the unitarity of its summands justify the norm estimate used in paper
   126	lines 1743-1750, independently of any strategy-consistency hypothesis. -/
   127	theorem norm_heteroKron_pauliCorrelation_apply_le {R : Type*}
   128	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R] (W : PauliKind)
   129	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × ((ι → K) × (ι → K)))) :
   130	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation W)) ψ‖ ≤ ‖ψ‖ := by
   131	  let U (u : ι → K) :=
   132	    heteroKron (1 : Op R) (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (tauObservable W u))
   133	  have hnorm (u : ι → K) :
   134	      ‖applyOperatorToState (U u) ψ‖ = ‖ψ‖ := by
   135	    apply MagicSquareRigidity.norm_toEuclideanLin_of_conjTranspose_mul_eq_one
   136	    simp only [U, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker,
   137	      Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
   138	    change heteroKron 1 (heteroKron (tauObservable W u)ᴴ (tauObservable W u)ᴴ) *
   139	      heteroKron 1 (heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (tauObservable W u)) = 1
   140	    rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, tauObservable_conjTranspose_mul_self,
   141	      heteroKron_one_one, Matrix.one_mul, heteroKron_one_one]
   142	  have haction : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation W)) ψ =
   143	      (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ • ∑ u : ι → K,
   144	        applyOperatorToState (U u) ψ := by
   145	    change applyOperatorToState
   146	      ((Matrix.kroneckerBilinear (R := ℂ) (α := ℂ) (1 : Op R))
   147	        ((Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   148	          ∑ u : ι → K, heteroKron (tauObservable W u) (tauObservable W u))) ψ = _
   149	    simp only [map_smul, map_sum, applyOperatorToState, LinearMap.sum_apply,
   150	      LinearMap.smul_apply]
   151	    rfl
   152	  rw [haction, norm_smul]
   153	  calc
   154	    _ ≤ ‖(Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹‖ * ∑ u : ι → K,
   155	        ‖applyOperatorToState (U u) ψ‖ :=
   156	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (norm_sum_le _ _) (norm_nonneg _)
   157	    _ = ‖ψ‖ := by
   158	      simp only [hnorm, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
   159	      rw [norm_inv, Complex.norm_natCast, ← mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel₀, one_mul]
   160	      positivity
   161	
   162	/-- Near-perfect X and Z correlations force proximity to the EPR subspace.
   163	This is the corrected projection estimate for paper lines 1743-1767, with
   164	arbitrary auxiliary registers. It uses the product identity and contraction
   165	bounds, and avoids the invalid squared-triangle estimate in the source. -/
   166	theorem norm_sub_eprProjection_le {R : Type*} [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
   167	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × ((ι → K) × (ι → K)))) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
   168	    (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
   169	    (hcorr : ∀ W : PauliKind,
   170	      1 - δ / 2 ≤ (inner ℂ ψ
   171	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation W)) ψ)).re) :
   172	    ‖ψ - applyOperatorToState
   173	      (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState (ι → K) x)
   174	        (fun y => star (eprState (ι → K) y)))) ψ‖ ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt δ := by
   175	  let H (W : PauliKind) := heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation (K := K) (ι := ι) W)
   176	  have hdist (W : PauliKind) : ‖ψ - applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ‖ ≤ Real.sqrt δ := by
   177	    have hn := norm_heteroKron_pauliCorrelation_apply_le W ψ
   178	    rw [hψ] at hn
   179	    have hs : ‖applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by
   180	      dsimp only [H]
   181	      nlinarith [norm_nonneg (applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)]
   182	    have he := norm_sub_sq (𝕜 := ℂ) ψ (applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)
   183	    rw [hψ] at he
   184	    change ‖ψ - applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ‖ ^ 2 =
   185	      1 ^ 2 - 2 * (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)).re +
   186	        ‖applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ‖ ^ 2 at he
   187	    have hc := hcorr W
   188	    change 1 - δ / 2 ≤ (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)).re at hc
   189	    nlinarith [Real.sq_sqrt hδ, Real.sqrt_nonneg δ,
   190	      norm_nonneg (ψ - applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)]
   191	  have hprod : H .X * H .Z =
   192	      heteroKron (1 : Op R) (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState (ι → K) x)
   193	        (fun y => star (eprState (ι → K) y))) := by
   194	    dsimp only [H]
   195	    rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, pauliCorrelation_mul_eq_epr]
   196	  rw [← hprod, DistanceCalculus.applyOperatorToState_mul]

   199	        ‖applyOperatorToState (H .X) ψ -
   200	          applyOperatorToState (H .X) (applyOperatorToState (H .Z) ψ)‖ :=
   201	      norm_sub_le_norm_sub_add_norm_sub _ _ _

   203	      rw [← MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_sub]
   204	      exact (norm_heteroKron_pauliCorrelation_apply_le .X _).trans (hdist .Z))

     4	/-!
     5	# The auxiliary vector from the EPR projection
     6	
     7	Taking the partial inner product with the EPR vector constructs the
     8	unnormalized auxiliary vector. Tensoring it with EPR gives exactly the
     9	orthogonal projection of the original vector onto the EPR subspace.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	Blueprint `lem:qld-unitary`; paper
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1769-1783`.
    15	-/

    25	/-- Move each extracted register before its auxiliary registers. This
    26	permutation puts the ideal state in the order used by
    27	`MagicSquareRigidity.exists_unit_residual`. -/
    28	def extractionEprFirstEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    29	    SixReg P ιA ιB ≃
    30	      (PauliRegister P × (ιA × PauliRegister P)) ×
    31	        (PauliRegister P × (ιB × PauliRegister P)) :=
    32	  (sixRegExtractionEquiv P ιA ιB).trans
    33	    (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.prodComm _ _) (Equiv.prodComm _ _))
    34	
    35	namespace Extraction
    36	
    37	/-- Partial inner product with the EPR vector, leaving the auxiliary index.
    38	This is the coordinate form of the vector defined at paper line 1769. -/
    39	def eprPartialInner {R V : Type*} [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    40	    [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V]
    41	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × (V × V))) : EuclideanSpace ℂ R :=
    42	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv R ℂ).symm
    43	    (fun r => ∑ p : V × V, star (eprState V p) * ψ (r, p))
    44	
    45	/-- Tensoring the EPR partial inner product with EPR gives the rank-one
    46	projection on the second tensor factor. This is the projection equality in
    47	paper lines 1776-1779; no normalization of the auxiliary vector is assumed. -/
    48	theorem vecTensor_eprPartialInner {R V : Type*} [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    49	    [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V]
    50	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × (V × V))) :
    51	    vecTensor (eprPartialInner ψ) (eprState V) =
    52	      applyOperatorToState
    53	        (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState V x)
    54	          (fun y => star (eprState V y)))) ψ := by
    55	  ext x
    56	  change (∑ p : V × V, star (eprState V p) * ψ (x.1, p)) * eprState V x.2 =
    57	    ∑ j : R × (V × V),
    58	      ((1 : Op R) x.1 j.1 * (eprState V x.2 * star (eprState V j.2))) * ψ j
    59	  conv_rhs => rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    60	  simp only [Matrix.one_apply, ite_mul, one_mul, zero_mul]
    61	  conv_rhs => rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    62	  simp only [Finset.sum_ite_eq, Finset.mem_univ, ite_true]
    63	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    64	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    65	  intro p _
    66	  ring
    67	
    68	end Extraction

    76	/-- In EPR-first local coordinates, the ideal extraction state is the target
    77	of the existing auxiliary-state normalization theorem. -/
    78	theorem reindexState_idealExpState
    79	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
    80	      (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
    81	    reindexState (extractionEprFirstEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    82	        (S.idealExpState aux) =
    83	      reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState (PauliRegister P)) aux) := by
    84	  ext index
    85	  change aux ((index.1.2.1, index.1.2.2), (index.2.2.1, index.2.2.2)) *
    86	      eprState (PauliRegister P) (index.1.1, index.2.1) =
    87	    eprState (PauliRegister P) (index.1.1, index.2.1) * aux (index.1.2, index.2.2)
    88	  exact mul_comm _ _
    89	
    90	/-- Tensoring an auxiliary vector with EPR preserves its norm. -/
    91	theorem idealExpState_norm
    92	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
    93	      (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
    94	    ‖S.idealExpState aux‖ = ‖aux‖ := by
    95	  rw [idealExpState, reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq, eprState_norm, mul_one]
    96	
    97	/-- A normalized reference vector on `AA'BB'`, formed from the original state
    98	and one EPR pair. It is used when the EPR projection of the given state vanishes. -/
    99	def extractionAuxReference : EuclideanSpace ℂ
   100	    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   101	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor S.toStrategy.ψ (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
   102	
   103	/-- The reference auxiliary vector has norm one. -/
   104	theorem extractionAuxReference_norm : ‖S.extractionAuxReference‖ = 1 := by
   105	  rw [extractionAuxReference, reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq, eprState_norm,
   106	    S.toStrategy.ψ_norm, one_mul]
   107	
   108	/-- The EPR projection on registers `A''B''`, with identity on `AA'BB'`.
   109	Paper lines 1766-1769 use this projection to select the auxiliary vector. -/
   110	def extractionEprProjection : Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   111	  reindexOp (extractionIdealShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB).symm
   112	    (heteroKron (1 : Op (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB))
   113	      (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState (PauliRegister P) x)
   114	        (fun y => star (eprState (PauliRegister P) y))))
   115	
   116	/-- The auxiliary vector before normalization, obtained by contracting the
   117	extracted registers against EPR. This is `aux_0` at paper line 1769. -/
   118	def extractionAux0
   119	    (θ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   120	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   121	  Extraction.eprPartialInner
   122	    (reindexState (extractionIdealShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB).symm θ)
   123	
   124	/-- The unnormalized ideal extraction state is the EPR projection of the
   125	given six-register state. This identifies the actual auxiliary construction
   126	with the projection in paper lines 1776-1779, retaining the heterogeneous
   127	player spaces of blueprint `lem:qld-unitary`. -/
   128	theorem idealExpState_extractionAux0
   129	    (θ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   130	    S.idealExpState (S.extractionAux0 θ) =
   131	      applyOperatorToState S.extractionEprProjection θ := by
   132	  unfold idealExpState extractionAux0
   133	  rw [Extraction.vecTensor_eprPartialInner]
   134	  ext x
   135	  let e := (extractionIdealShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB).symm
   136	  let T := heteroKron
   137	    (1 : Op (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB))
   138	    (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState (PauliRegister P) x)
   139	      (fun y => star (eprState (PauliRegister P) y)))
   140	  change (T *ᵥ (fun j => θ (e.symm j))) (e x) =
   141	    ((T.submatrix e e) *ᵥ (fun j => θ j)) x
   142	  exact (congrFun (Matrix.submatrix_mulVec_equiv T (fun j => θ j) e e) x).symm
   143	
   144	/-- Normalize the projected auxiliary vector, at twice the projection error.
   145	This is the normalization step at paper lines 1773-1783. The existing
   146	normalization theorem also covers a zero projection, using the reference
   147	vector above; no nonvanishing assumption is added. -/
   148	theorem exists_unit_aux_near_eprProjection
   149	    (θ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) (hθ : ‖θ‖ = 1) :
   150	    ∃ aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB),
   151	      ‖aux‖ = 1 ∧ ‖θ - S.idealExpState aux‖ ≤
   152	        2 * ‖θ - applyOperatorToState S.extractionEprProjection θ‖ := by
   153	  let e := extractionEprFirstEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB
   154	  have hdist (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
   155	      (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   156	      ‖reindexState e θ -
   157	        reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState (PauliRegister P)) aux)‖ =
   158	          ‖θ - S.idealExpState aux‖ := by
   159	    rw [← S.reindexState_idealExpState]
   160	    exact (LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrLeft 2 ℂ ℂ e).norm_map (θ - S.idealExpState aux)
   161	  obtain ⟨aux, haux, hclose⟩ := MagicSquareRigidity.exists_unit_residual
   162	    (reindexState e θ) (by rwa [reindexState_norm_eq])
   163	    S.extractionAuxReference S.extractionAuxReference_norm
   164	    ‖θ - applyOperatorToState S.extractionEprProjection θ‖ (S.extractionAux0 θ)
   165	    (((hdist (S.extractionAux0 θ)).trans
   166	      (congrArg (fun v => ‖θ - v‖) (S.idealExpState_extractionAux0 θ))).le)
   167	  exact ⟨aux, haux, (hdist aux).symm.trans_le hclose⟩
   168

    33	theorem avg_norm_fixed_character_sum_sq {P : AdmissibleParams} {E : Type*}

    35	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) (fun r =>
    36	      ‖∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (r * a)) • v a‖ ^ 2) =
    37	      ∑ a, ‖v a‖ ^ 2 := by

    39	  have horth (a b : PauliScalar P) :
    40	      ∑ r : PauliScalar P,
    41	        (starRingEnd ℂ) (phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (r * a))) *
    42	          phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (r * b)) =
    43	        if a = b then ((Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℝ) : ℂ) else 0 := by
    44	    simpa only [← Complex.star_def, star_phaseSign, Complex.ofReal_natCast] using

    47	    sum_norm_sum_smul_sq_of_orthogonal _ _ horth v, ← mul_assoc,

    53	theorem avg_norm_basis_character_sum_sq {P : AdmissibleParams} {E : Type*}
    54	    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E]
    55	    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) (v : PauliScalar P → E) :
    56	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) (fun r =>
    57	      ‖∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * r * a)) • v a‖ ^ 2) =
    58	      ∑ a, ‖v a‖ ^ 2 := by
    59	  classical
    60	  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum]
    61	  have hsum := Equiv.sum_comp
    62	    (Equiv.mulLeft₀ (P.model.basis j) (P.model.basis.ne_zero j))

    65	    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * r * a)) • v a‖ ^ 2) = _ at hsum

    72	theorem sum_basis_character_effect_eq {P : AdmissibleParams} {ι : Type*}

    74	    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :

    77	        (A.postprocess (fun a => fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a))).effect b := by

    80	    (g := fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a))

    85	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    86	  intro a ha

    89	/-- A fixed basis character costs at most four times the field measurement

    92	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, without assuming a bound on that defect. -/
    93	theorem basis_character_opDistSq_le_four_consistencyDefect
    94	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {X ιA ιB : Type*}
    95	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    96	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    97	    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement (PauliScalar P) ιA)
    98	    (B : X → Measurement (PauliScalar P) ιB)
    99	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :

   102	        (∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)) • (A x).effect a) 1)

   104	        (∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)) • (B x).effect a)) ψ ≤

   108	  let f := fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)

   110	  let B' := fun x => (B x).postprocess f

   114	    (fun x => rightPlacedMeasurement (B' x)) ψ).trans

   118	    (fun x => rightPlacedMeasurement (B' x)) phaseSign norm_phaseSign ψ

   120	  have hbound := hobs.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hfam (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2))
   121	  simpa only [sum_basis_character_effect_eq, heteroKron_left_sum_smul,
   122	    heteroKron_right_sum_smul, leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement,
   123	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne, ← mul_assoc, show (2 : ℝ) * 2 = 4 by norm_num]
   124	    using hbound

   126	/-- The final measurement-to-observable step of blueprint
   127	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, Item 2, on the original six-register state.

   131	theorem tildeObs_opDistSq_le_four_consistencyDefect
   132	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
   133	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
   134	    (W : PauliKind) (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
   135	    opDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   136	      (fun u => S.placeSide .alice (tildeObs w .alice W u j))
   137	      (fun u => S.placeSide .bob (tildeObs w .bob W u j)) S.psiHat ≤
   138	      4 * consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   139	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice (tildeM w .alice W u a))
   140	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W u a)) S.psiHat := by
   141	  classical
   142	  let M (side : PlayerSide) (u : PauliRegister P) :
   143	      Measurement (PauliScalar P) (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
   144	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne (tildeM w side W u)
   145	      (fun a => (tildeM_isProj w side W u a).nonneg) (sum_tildeM_eq_one w side W u)
   146	  let e := sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB
   147	  have h := basis_character_opDistSq_le_four_consistencyDefect
   148	    (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P)) (M .alice) (M .bob)
   149	    (reindexState e S.psiHat) j
   150	  have hd : opDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   151	      (fun u => heteroKron (tildeObs w .alice W u j) 1)
   152	      (fun u => heteroKron 1 (tildeObs w .bob W u j)) (reindexState e S.psiHat) =
   153	      opDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   154	        (fun u => S.placeSide .alice (tildeObs w .alice W u j))
   155	        (fun u => S.placeSide .bob (tildeObs w .bob W u j)) S.psiHat := by
   156	    unfold opDistSq opFamilyDistSq
   157	    simp only [Fintype.sum_unique]
   158	    apply avgOver_congr
   159	    intro u
   160	    rw [norm_applyOperatorToState_reindexState, reindexOp_sub]
   161	    rfl
   162	  have hc : consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   163	      (fun u a => heteroKron (tildeM w .alice W u a) 1)
   164	      (fun u a => heteroKron 1 (tildeM w .bob W u a)) (reindexState e S.psiHat) =
   165	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   166	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice (tildeM w .alice W u a))
   167	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W u a)) S.psiHat := by
   168	    unfold consistencyDefect
   169	    apply avgOver_congr
   170	    intro u
   171	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   172	    intro a _
   173	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   174	    intro b _
   175	    by_cases hab : a = b
   176	    · simp only [hab, if_true]
   177	    · simp only [if_neg hab, consistency_term_eq_stateQForm]
   178	      rw [stateQForm_reindexState, reindexOp_mul]
   179	      rfl
   180	  change opDistSq _ (fun u => heteroKron (tildeObs w .alice W u j) 1)
   181	    (fun u => heteroKron 1 (tildeObs w .bob W u j)) _ ≤
   182	      4 * consistencyDefect _ (fun u a => heteroKron (tildeM w .alice W u a) 1)
   183	        (fun u a => heteroKron 1 (tildeM w .bob W u a)) _ at h

# Lean Proof Integrity Rules

This file is the **single source of truth** for proof integrity checks in this
repository. All CI workflows and review prompts should reference this file
rather than duplicating the rules inline.

> **Lean version**: 4.x (Lean 3 keywords like `constant` do not apply)

> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues
> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check below yet still
> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,
> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default
> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).
> Consult it alongside this file during review.

> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a
> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`
> blocker below may be temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The
> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof
> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the
> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a
> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or
> conditional helper
> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.
> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge
> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.

---

## Blockers

These patterns **must** be resolved before merging.

### Direct proof holes

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `sorry` | Axiomatically closes any goal — the proof is incomplete |
| `admit` | Tactic alias for `sorry` |

### Kernel / type system bypasses

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `native_decide` | Relies on trusted native evaluation / compiler; banned in Mathlib for soundness and process reasons |
| `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce` | Type system bypass — can fabricate any proof term |
| `lcProof` | Low-level proof fabrication primitive — can prove `False` |
| `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat` | Kernel reduction primitives exploitable for unsound proofs |

### Axiom smuggling

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `axiom` declarations | Introduces unproven assumptions that could be inconsistent; must be explicitly justified |

When an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,
prefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`
declaration, and add a regression check (for example a
`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen
the axiomatic base.

This preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper
theorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a
caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a
proof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly
conditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement
faithful to the paper.

### Circular reasoning

Lean's kernel forbids literal declaration cycles, so focus on **mathematical
circularity**:

- Proofs that assume (or trivially reintroduce) the statement being proved as a
  local hypothesis, then immediately close the goal from that hypothesis
- Helper lemmas in the same file that essentially restate the main goal and are
  only used to prove that goal
- Local `have`/`let` bindings that are just the goal rephrased, used to solve
  the goal without any real argument
- Newly introduced `axiom` that makes a difficult statement trivially provable
  without connecting to existing Mathlib / core theorems
- Abuse of `unsafe` features to fabricate proofs instead of giving a genuine
  derivation
- `by exact h` where `h` came from an unjustified assumption identical to the
  goal

### Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)

Proofs that avoid grounding in Mathlib:

- Custom re-declarations of standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., re-proving
  `add_comm` instead of importing it)
- `axiom` or `sorry`-based helper lemmas for facts that already exist in
  Mathlib
- Chains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core
- `private` helper lemmas that duplicate Mathlib API (e.g., custom matrix
  transpose lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)
- Overly long proof chains replaceable by a single Mathlib lemma

When flagging, perform an actual lookup (grep, `#find?`, `exact?`,
`library_search`). If an equivalent exists, cite the Mathlib lemma and module
path. If not, state "no equivalent found" with search evidence.

### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization

This is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or
theorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,
making them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.

Signs to watch for:

- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,
  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's
  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)
- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types
  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions
- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical
  semantics (e.g., a "projective measurement" definition that does not enforce
  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)
- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be
  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything
- Definitions that "work" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to
  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,
  incompatible universes)

When reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of
this?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the
scaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks
progress rather than enabling it.

### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift

A theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker
if its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.
Changing a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
documented mathematical necessity.

The most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an
extra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional
theorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not
repair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named
`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,
generic `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those
assumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.

Conditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet
be closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a
named lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional
helper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named
obligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show
that it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or
`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled
blueprint theorem with `\leanok`.

Existing bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs
for reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a
strengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the
bridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is
to restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a
tracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.

Not every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed
to encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model
instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be
faithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These
conditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is
mathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate
step of the source proof.

For every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:

- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;
- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;
- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened
  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.

---

## Warnings

These should be flagged for review but may be acceptable with justification.

### Placeholder tactics

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`, `suggest` | Search tactics left as placeholders — replace with the concrete result |

### Safety / termination bypasses

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `unsafe def` | Bypasses Lean safety checks; should not appear in proof-relevant code |
| `partial def` | No termination proof required; unsound if used to build proof terms |
| `implemented_by` / `implementedBy` | Decouples runtime behavior from proven specification |

### Suspicious options

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `set_option maxHeartbeats 0` | Disables timeout — can hide non-terminating proofs |
| `set_option maxHeartbeats` with values >= 4,000,000 | 20x the default (200,000) — likely indicates an inefficient proof |
| `set_option maxRecDepth` with values >= 10,000 | May hide structural issues in proofs |

### Debug artifacts

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `dbg_trace` | Debug trace left in code |
| `stop` | Halts elaboration — development aid only |
| `#check`, `#eval`, `#print` in proof files | Debug commands that should be removed |

---

## How to use this file

**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read
[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a
proof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation
structure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why
conditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a
tracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.

**In CI review prompts**: Reference this file instead of inlining the rules:
```
Read `docs/PROOF_INTEGRITY.md` for the complete list of proof integrity
rules. Flag blockers as must-fix issues that should block merge.
Flag warnings as advisory — note them but acknowledge they may be
acceptable with justification.
```

**For manual review**: Use this as a checklist when reviewing Lean PRs.

**Updating rules**: Edit this file and all referencing workflows will
automatically pick up the changes.

\section{The swap unitaries and the extraction of the Pauli group}

\begin{definition}[The swap unitaries]\label{def:v-swap-unitary}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary}
	\leanok
	\uses{lem:qld-4-7, def:generalized-pauli, def:qld-full-field-decoder}
	Define the linear map
	\[
		V_{\mathrm{A}} = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \bigl(\tau^X(\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \, \tau^Z(\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}''}\;,
	\]
	where $\tau^X(\cdot)$ and $\tau^Z(\cdot)$ are the generalized Pauli observables acting on $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$; note that the argument of $\tau^X$ is $\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\tau^Z$ is $\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)$. The map $V_{\mathrm{B}}$, acting on registers $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, is defined analogously.
\end{definition}

% In the source the following properties are established inline with the
% definition of the swap unitaries; they are recorded here as a lemma.
\begin{lemma}[Unitarity and conjugation action of the swap unitaries]\label{lem:v-swap-conjugation}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.conjTranspose_mul_swapUnitary}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_conj_tildeObs}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_conj_tildeM}
	\leanok
	\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, def:tilde-w-observables, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:generalized-pauli, def:indicator-vector, def:bracket}
	The maps $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{B}}$ of Definition~\ref{def:v-swap-unitary} are unitaries acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$ respectively, and their conjugation action is exact, as follows. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $j \in \{0,\ldots,t-1\}$, and $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M$,
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}
		V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \bigl( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \bigr)_{\mathrm{A}''}
		\qquad \text{and} \qquad
		V_{\mathrm{B}} \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot \bigl( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \bigr)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
	\end{equation}
	and for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^m$, and $a \in \F_q$,
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
		V_{\mathrm{B}} \, \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \, V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
		\qquad
		\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h \,:\, g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_h\;,
	\end{equation}
	together with the analogous identity for $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\uses{lem:qld-4-7, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:twisted-commutation, def:v-swap-unitary, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:tau-dot-product-projector, def:indicator-vector, def:decoding-map, def:generalized-pauli}
	Since the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ is projective (Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}) and the $\tau^X, \tau^Z$ observables are self-inverse,
	\[
		V_{\mathrm{A}} V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \Id_{\mathrm{A}''} = \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}\;,
	\]
	and the same computation gives $V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger V_{\mathrm{A}} = \Id$, so $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ is unitary; likewise $V_{\mathrm{B}}$. For \eqref{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}, conjugate the product form \eqref{eq:tildewj-product-form} of $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}): by the orthogonality of the projectors $\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$, only the diagonal terms survive, and the twisted commutation relation (Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation})
	\[
		\tau^X(\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \, \tau^Z(\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)) \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \, \tau^X(\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \, \tau^Z(\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))
	\]
	cancels the sign $(-1)^{\tr(e_j (\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))}$ term by term, leaving $\sum_{g_X,g_Z} \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z} \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \Id \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})$. For \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, expand $\tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$ by \eqref{eq:tilde_M} and \eqref{eq:def-tauwu}; by the orthogonality of the $\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$, conjugation replaces, in the term of $\hat{S}^W_g$, each projector $\tau^W_h$ by $\tau^W_{h + \mathrm{Dec}(g)}$, using the identities $\tau^X(s)\, \tau^Z_h \,\tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h+s}$ and $\tau^Z(s)\, \tau^X_h\, \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h+s}$. Substituting $h' = h + \mathrm{Dec}(g)$ turns the constraint $h \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = (\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)) - a$ into $h' \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = -a = a$, since $\F_q$ has characteristic $2$; the quantity $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ cancels exactly, so no relation between it and $g(u)$ is used (Remark~\ref{rem:qld-decoding-identity}). Since $h' \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g_{h'}(u)$ \eqref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}, summing over $g$ gives \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}; the computation for $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ is identical.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Extraction of the EPR state and the Pauli observables]\label{lem:qld-unitary}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ExtractionWitness}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaExtract}
	\uses{lem:qld-4-7, def:v-swap-unitary, def:expanded-state, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
	There is a universal constant $C_{\mathrm{ext}}\geq1$. Set
	\[
		\delta_P^{\mathrm{ext}}=C_{\mathrm{ext}}B,
		\qquad
		\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}=C_{\mathrm{ext}}
		\left((\delta_P^{\mathrm{ext}})^{1/4}+\frac{md}{q}\right).
	\]
	There exist unitaries $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $V_{\mathrm{B}}$ acting on registers $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, such that the following hold.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item There exists a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ such that
		\[
			\bigl\| V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}}_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \bigr\|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
		\]
		\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
		\begin{align*}
			V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \bigl(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \bigr)_{\mathrm{A}} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''}\;, \\
			V_{\mathrm{B}} \, \bigl(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \bigr)_{\mathrm{B}} \, V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
		\end{align*}
		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''}$, with the answer summation over $h \in \F_q^{M}$ and no average over questions.
	\end{enumerate}
	The unitaries may be taken to be $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{B}}$ of Definition~\ref{def:v-swap-unitary}.
	The conditional result below assumes the global polynomial-pair measurement
	of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, whereas the present proof obtains that measurement
	from the lemma. It therefore establishes the extraction conclusions only
	after the measurement and its consistency estimates are supplied, not the
	existence claim above. The missing composition and the range-projection
	transfer are recorded in \cite{gap:qpbt_extraction-transfer}.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, lem:v-swap-conjugation, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:qld-construct-the-paulis, lem:qld-win-implications, fact:triangle-for-simeq, def:bracket, lem:cancellation, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree, lem:qld-4-7}
	For the first item, the self-consistency of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ (Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}) is equivalent, since these observables are Hermitian involutions (Lemma~\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}), to $\E_{j \in \{0,\ldots,t-1\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M} \bra{\hat\psi} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ot \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat\psi} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$; setting $\ket{\vartheta} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$ and using the exact conjugation identities of Lemma~\ref{lem:v-swap-conjugation}, this becomes $\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$, where $H_W = \E_j \E_{\tilde{u}} \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \bigl( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \ot \tau^W(s) \bigr)^{\ot M}$ by the tensor factorization of $\tau^W(\tilde{u})$ and the invariance of the uniform average over $s$ under $s \mapsto e_j s$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:cancellation}, $\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \ot \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ on each pair of qudits, whence $H_X H_Z = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$. The bounds $\| (\Id - H_W)\ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq \delta_P$ and $\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_P$, combined through the triangle inequality $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ (see Remark~\ref{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}), give $\bra{\vartheta} \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 4\delta_P$.
	% Case distinction added: the source normalizes the projected vector
	% without ensuring that it is nonzero; see Remark rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip.
	If $\delta_P > 1/8$, then, after enlarging the universal constant in $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, both items of the lemma hold with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ an arbitrary unit state, since their left-hand sides never exceed $4$; assume therefore $\delta_P \leq 1/8$. Then the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ has squared norm at least $1 - 4\delta_P \geq 1/2 > 0$, and $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ may be defined as its normalization; the overlap of $\ket{\vartheta}$ with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ equals the norm of that vector and is at least $\sqrt{1 - 4\delta_P} \geq 1 - 4\delta_P$, which yields the first item with a bound of $8\delta_P = O(\sqrt{\delta_P})$. For the second item, Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} gives, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$, $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ and $\Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \simeq_\eps M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \Id$, where $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h$; combining these with Item~1 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} by Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle-for-simeq}, using $\eps \leq \sqrt{\eps} \leq \delta_P$, yields $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}} \Id \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$. Writing $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, the quantity to be bounded for the $\mathrm{A}$-side relation equals $2 - 2\sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_{\mathrm{A}} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \ot (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\Delta}$, since $(\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} = (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$. Replacing $(\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}$ by the averaged coarse-graining $\E_u \sum_{h' : g_{h'}(u) = g_h(u)} (\tau^W_{h'})_{\mathrm{B}''}$ costs at most $md/q$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} (distinct $h \neq h'$ have distinct encodings $g_h \neq g_{h'}$, of total degree at most $md$), and by \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6} the resulting sum equals $\E_u \sum_{a} \bra{\Delta} V_{\mathrm{A}} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \ket{\Delta}$. Exchanging $\ket{\Delta}$ for $\ket{\vartheta}$ costs $O(\delta_P^{1/4})$ by the first item, and the resulting expression $\E_u \sum_a \bra{\hat\psi} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat\psi}$ is at least $1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_P})$ by the $\simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}}$ relation above. Altogether the distance is $O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$; the $\mathrm{B}$-side relation is proved identically.
\end{proof}

One may take `a' = 4 * C^2 * a` and `b' = b / 8`. Subadditivity of the
fourth root bounds the three construction terms separately. Admissibility
gives `md ≥ 1` and `q ≥ 1`, so their polynomial factors and the term `md/q`

theorem deltaExtract_le_deltaQld (C a b : ℝ) (hC : 1 ≤ C) (ha : 1 < a)
    (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b < 1) :
    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' < 1 ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon : ℝ), 0 ≤ epsilon →
        epsilon ≤ 1 →
        deltaExtract C
            (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
              (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q)
            P.m P.d P.q ≤
          deltaQld a' b' epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by
  have hC0 : 0 ≤ C := by linarith
  have ha0 : 0 ≤ a := by linarith
  have hconstant : a ≤ 4 * C ^ 2 * a := by
    have hCsq : 1 ≤ C ^ 2 := by nlinarith
    nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hCsq ha0]
  refine ⟨4 * C ^ 2 * a, b / 8, ha.le.trans hconstant, by positivity, by linarith, ?_⟩
  intro params epsilon hepsilon0 hepsilon1
  let degree : ℝ := ((params.m * params.d : ℕ) : ℝ)
  have hdegree1 : 1 ≤ degree :=
    Nat.one_le_cast.mpr (Nat.mul_pos params.one_le_m params.hd)
  have hdegree0 : 0 ≤ degree := by linarith
  have hfield1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (params.q : ℝ) := by
    obtain ⟨size, -, hsize⟩ := params.hq
    rw [hsize]
    exact_mod_cast Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by norm_num)
  have hfield0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (params.q : ℝ) := by positivity
  let amplitude : ℝ := a * degree ^ a
  let rate : ℝ := epsilon ^ (b / 8) + (params.q : ℝ) ^ (-(b / 8)) +
    (2 : ℝ) ^ (-((b / 8) * degree))
  have hamplitude1 : 1 ≤ amplitude :=
    one_le_mul_of_one_le_of_one_le ha.le (Real.one_le_rpow hdegree1 ha0)
  have hamplitude0 : 0 ≤ amplitude := by linarith
  have hdegree_amplitude : degree ≤ amplitude :=
    (Real.self_le_rpow_of_one_le hdegree1 ha.le).trans
      (le_mul_of_one_le_left (Real.rpow_nonneg hdegree0 a) ha.le)
  have hrate0 : 0 ≤ rate := by dsimp [rate]; positivity
  have hepsilon_rate : epsilon ^ (b / 8) ≤ rate := by
    dsimp [rate]
    linarith [Real.rpow_nonneg hfield0 (-(b / 8)),
      Real.rpow_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2) (-((b / 8) * degree))]
  have hfield_rate : (params.q : ℝ) ^ (-(b / 8)) ≤ rate := by
    dsimp [rate]
    linarith [Real.rpow_nonneg hepsilon0 (b / 8),
      Real.rpow_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2) (-((b / 8) * degree))]
  have hroot_sum {first second third : ℝ}
      (hfirst : 0 ≤ first) (hsecond : 0 ≤ second) (hthird : 0 ≤ third) :
      (first + second + third) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤
        first ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) + second ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) + third ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) :=
    (Real.rpow_add_le_add_rpow (p := (1 / 4 : ℝ)) (add_nonneg hfirst hsecond) hthird
      (by norm_num) (by norm_num)).trans
      (add_le_add (Real.rpow_add_le_add_rpow (p := (1 / 4 : ℝ)) hfirst hsecond
        (by norm_num) (by norm_num)) le_rfl)
  have hrate_root :
      (epsilon ^ b + (params.q : ℝ) ^ (-b) + (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * degree))) ^
        (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ rate := by
    refine (hroot_sum (by positivity) (by positivity) (by positivity)).trans ?_
    rw [← Real.rpow_mul hepsilon0, ← Real.rpow_mul hfield0,
      ← Real.rpow_mul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)]
    refine add_le_add (add_le_add ?_ ?_) ?_
    · exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hepsilon0 hepsilon1
        (by positivity) (by linarith)
    · exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hfield1 (by linarith)
    · apply Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by norm_num)
      nlinarith [mul_nonneg hb.le hdegree0]
  have hglobal0 : 0 ≤ deltaQld a b epsilon params.m params.d params.q := by
    simp only [deltaQld, Real.rpow_eq_pow]
    positivity
  have hglobal_root :
      (deltaQld a b epsilon params.m params.d params.q) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤
        amplitude * rate := by
    change (amplitude *
      (epsilon ^ b + (params.q : ℝ) ^ (-b) + (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * degree)))) ^
        (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ amplitude * rate
    rw [Real.mul_rpow hamplitude0 (by positivity)]
    exact mul_le_mul (Real.rpow_le_self_of_one_le hamplitude1 (by norm_num))
      hrate_root (by positivity) hamplitude0
  have hsqrt_root : (Real.sqrt epsilon) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ amplitude * rate := by
    rw [Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, ← Real.rpow_mul hepsilon0]
    exact ((Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hepsilon0 hepsilon1
      (by positivity) (by linarith)).trans hepsilon_rate).trans
      (le_mul_of_one_le_left hrate0 hamplitude1)
  have hratio_root : (degree / (params.q : ℝ)) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ amplitude * rate := by
    rw [Real.div_rpow hdegree0 hfield0, div_eq_mul_inv, ← Real.rpow_neg hfield0]
    exact mul_le_mul
      ((Real.rpow_le_self_of_one_le hdegree1 (by norm_num)).trans hdegree_amplitude)
      ((Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hfield1 (by linarith)).trans hfield_rate)
      (by positivity) hamplitude0
  have hratio : degree / (params.q : ℝ) ≤ amplitude * rate := by
    rw [div_eq_mul_inv, ← Real.rpow_neg_one]
    exact mul_le_mul hdegree_amplitude
      ((Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hfield1 (by linarith)).trans hfield_rate)
      (by positivity) hamplitude0
  have hconstruct_root :
      (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
        (deltaQld a b epsilon params.m params.d params.q) params.m params.d params.q) ^
          (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ 3 * C * amplitude * rate := by
    unfold deltaConstructPaulis
    rw [Real.mul_rpow hC0 (by positivity)]
    calc
      C ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) *
          (deltaQld a b epsilon params.m params.d params.q + Real.sqrt epsilon +
            degree / (params.q : ℝ)) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤
          C * ((deltaQld a b epsilon params.m params.d params.q) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) +
            (Real.sqrt epsilon) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) +
            (degree / (params.q : ℝ)) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) :=
        mul_le_mul (Real.rpow_le_self_of_one_le hC (by norm_num))
          (hroot_sum hglobal0 (by positivity) (by positivity))
          (by positivity) hC0
      _ ≤ C * (amplitude * rate + amplitude * rate + amplitude * rate) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
          (add_le_add (add_le_add hglobal_root hsqrt_root) hratio_root) hC0
      _ = 3 * C * amplitude * rate := by ring
  calc
    deltaExtract C
        (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
          (deltaQld a b epsilon params.m params.d params.q) params.m params.d params.q)
        params.m params.d params.q ≤
        C * (3 * C * amplitude * rate + amplitude * rate) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (add_le_add hconstruct_root hratio) hC0
    _ = (C * (3 * C + 1)) * (amplitude * rate) := by ring
    _ ≤ 4 * C ^ 2 * (amplitude * rate) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by nlinarith) (mul_nonneg hamplitude0 hrate0)
    _ = (4 * C ^ 2 * a) * degree ^ a * rate := by dsimp [amplitude]; ring
    _ ≤ deltaQld (4 * C ^ 2 * a) (b / 8) epsilon params.m params.d params.q :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
        (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
          (Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hdegree1 hconstant) (by positivity)) hrate0

end

  passing from unitary conjugation to isometry conjugation.
  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} A corrected positive-contraction estimate,

  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Positivity, contraction inequalities,

  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The inequality

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
\[
  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
\]
Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
\[
  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
  \qquad
  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
\]
Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
\[
  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
\]
Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.

For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
\[
  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
\]
not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
$\Delta$.

\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}

Lines~1715--1742 of
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.

The triangle inequality yields
\[
  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
\]
so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.

\section{The range-projection obligation}

Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.

Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
\[
  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
\]
where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.

This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.

\section{Blueprint and formalization status}

The proof of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} and the soundness proof in
\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} use the corrected
positive-contraction estimate, make the small-error case distinction explicit,
and isolate the range-projection calculation.  The chapter therefore preserves
the source's state and observable conclusions while exposing the omitted
argument.

The structure \path{ExtractionWitness} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Unitary.lean} contains only the two-sided
unitarity equations for the concrete swap maps, a normalized auxiliary state,
the transformed-state estimate, and the two-player Pauli-projector comparison.
The theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness_ofGlobalPairWitness} concludes the
existence of this data at the explicit extraction scale, but it takes the
\path{GlobalPairWitness} of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-7} as an explicit hypothesis
rather than obtaining it from \path{exists_globalPairWitness}.  That bundle
carries the projective global polynomial-pair measurements and both
point-consistency estimates, and the blueprint proof of
Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} obtains it from Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-7}; deleting
the hypothesis would leave that construction unproved.  By the criterion of
\path{docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex} the hypothesis is therefore proof
debt rather than a faithful boundary condition, and the declaration is a
conditional helper: it does not certify the source lemma, and the blueprint
node Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} accordingly neither links it nor carries any
statement-level formalization mark.  The declaration is recorded instead on the
separate formalization-support node
\path{lem:qld-unitary-given-global-pair}, whose statement assumes the global
polynomial-pair measurement explicitly and whose formal link points only to the
conditional helper.  The helper is proved at this conditional statement and
has only the standard axioms \path{propext}, \path{Classical.choice}, and
\path{Quot.sound}; the support node records the matching statement without
identifying it as the source result.  Apart from that hypothesis the
conclusion matches the Stage~4.2 extraction lemma, including the corrected
numerical estimates; the later passage to the isometries in the soundness
theorem is not formalized, and no declaration yet states that passage.

The conditional character of the result is visible wherever the declaration is
invoked: the suffix \path{ofGlobalPairWitness} names the extra premise in the
declaration itself, and its docstring records the statement as conditional and
its dependence on the assumed witness as unfaithful.  Discharging the debt
requires composing \path{exists_globalPairWitness} with this helper to obtain
the source lemma.  The source-facing theorem
\path{exists_pulled_apart_consistency} now states the preceding global-measurement
construction and its three consistency estimates without a witness premise,
but its tracked proof remains open because the current
\path{exists_globalPairWitness} is unfinished and excludes zero error.  No
declaration carries out the source witness/extraction composition.

Issue~\#19 owns this concrete Stage~4.2 interface and discrepancy record.
\ghissue{123} owns the source-facing composition through
\path{exists_globalPairWitness}.  \ghissue{47} tracks the separate
range-projection transfer needed by \path{pauli_soundness}; that theorem must
be derived from the concrete data rather than stored in the witness.

\section{Conclusion}

The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
already supplied by the extraction lemma.  Independently of both defects, the
present extraction declaration is conditional on the global polynomial-pair
measurement, and that conditionality must be removed before it may be
advertised as the source lemma.
