\title{The Decoding Identity in the Pauli Extraction Argument}
\author{}
\date{2026-09-03}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{At a glance}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source applies a decoder--encoder
  identity to every bounded individual-degree polynomial, although the identity
  is guaranteed for encoded polynomials and can fail outside the encoding image.
  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One restricted algebraic identity and one
  probabilistic estimate showing that the constructed measurement assigns
  little state-dependent mass to outcomes outside the encoding image.
  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Evaluation of the multilinear
  interpolant is elementary polynomial algebra.  The non-encoding-mass bound
  uses project-specific consistency estimates and Schwartz--Zippel.
  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Multilinear interpolation on the
  Boolean cube, injectivity of the low-degree encoding, measurement
  consistency, and Schwartz--Zippel.  The correction is tracked in
  \ghissue{19}.
\end{itemize}

\section{Key theorem forms}

For a word $h\colon\{0,1\}^m\to\mathbb F_q$, let $g_h$ be its multilinear
extension.  Define the chapter's decoder by
\[
  \operatorname{Dec}(g)(y)=g(y),
  \qquad y\in\{0,1\}^m.
\]
Then
\[
  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g_h(u).
\]
More generally, the second identity holds for a polynomial outcome $g$ under
the explicit hypothesis that $g$ belongs to the image of the encoding; no
converse is asserted.

For an arbitrary bounded individual-degree polynomial $g$, the Boolean values
determine its multilinear interpolant, not necessarily $g$ itself.  The
unrestricted identity
\[
  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g(u)
\]
is therefore false.

\section{Counterexample and source comparison}

The low-degree encoding is defined at lines~873--897 of
\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}.  The general decoder at
lines~917--924 retains evaluations lying in a chosen subset $H$; the extraction
chapter instead specifies at lines~1419--1420 of
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} that the
decoder returns all evaluations on the Boolean cube.  This is the specialization
$H=\mathbb F_q$, rather than the Boolean-valued shorthand used earlier
\cite[lines~873--924 and 1419--1420]{Ji2020MIPStar}.

Take $m=1$, $d\geq2$, and a field of characteristic two with more than two
elements.  For $g(x)=x^2$, the Boolean evaluations are $g(0)=0$ and $g(1)=1$.
Consequently the decoder is the word whose multilinear extension is $x$.
For any $u\notin\{0,1\}$ with $u^2\neq u$,
\[
  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_1(u)=u
  \neq u^2=g(u).
\]
Thus the equality asserted for every $g$ at lines~1483--1492 of the chapter-14
source mirror is false \cite[lines~1483--1492]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  If degrees at
least $q$ are allowed, equality as a function would not by itself prove encoding
membership either, since $x^q$ and $x$ induce the same function on $\mathbb F_q$.

\section{Required repair}

The extraction proof must split the marginal measurement into encoding and
non-encoding outcomes.  On encoding outcomes, the restricted identity above
justifies the substitution.  On the complement, the proof must bound
\[
  \sum_{g\ \mathrm{not\ an\ encoding}}
  \langle\widehat\psi,\widehat S_g^W\widehat\psi\rangle.
\]
The blueprint derives an $O(\delta_S)+md/q$ bound from point consistency and
the combined point measurement.  A non-encoding polynomial differs from every
encoded polynomial, so Schwartz--Zippel bounds the probability that their
evaluations coincide.  This estimate is the open reduction; it must be proved
from the paper hypotheses rather than inserted as an extraction hypothesis.

The printed reindexing at lines~1805--1822 replaces
$g_{\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)}$ by $g_W$, which is the invalid reverse identity
for an arbitrary polynomial outcome.  In the corrected calculation, the
constraint is
$g_h(u)=\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)-a$.
After setting $h'=h+\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)$, the defining evaluation formula
$g_k(u)=k\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)$ and characteristic two turn
that constraint into $g_{h'}(u)=a$.  Thus this step uses neither decoder
linearity nor the identity $\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h$
\cite[lines~1805--1822]{Ji2020MIPStar}.

\section{Blueprint and formalization status}

Definition~\path{def:qld-full-field-decoder} and
Lemmas~\path{lem:qld-decoder-linearity} and
\path{lem:qld-decoder-evaluation} in
\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} state the full-field
decoder, its linearity and inverse, and the evaluation identity restricted to
encoding outcomes.  Lemma~\path{lem:qld-nonencoding-mass-bound}
separately records the estimate on the remaining outcomes.

The declarations \path{decodeFq_add}, \path{decodeFq_smul}, and
\path{decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Decoding.lean} match the three algebraic assertions.
In the same file, \path{IsEncoding} is the equality
$g_{\operatorname{Dec}(g)}=g$ of polynomial representatives, and
\path{decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec} requires an explicit hypothesis
of that predicate.  It therefore matches the corrected evaluation lemma and
does not assert the false unrestricted identity.  Finally,
\path{nonencodingMarginalMass_le} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Consistency.lean} concludes the complementary
mass bound from the projective strategy and global polynomial-pair witness; it
does not add the bound as a witness field or theorem hypothesis.

The decoder calculations are proved.  \path{lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly},
\path{decodeFq_add}, \path{decodeFq_smul}, \path{decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding},
and \path{decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec} carry complete proofs: the degree
side-condition on $g_h$, the two linearity laws, the inversion
$\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathbb F_q}(g_h)=h$, and the evaluation identity under the
explicit \path{IsEncoding} hypothesis.  The complementary estimate
\path{nonencodingMarginalMass_le} is the remaining open proof of this note.
Issue~\#19 owns the Stage~4.2 statements and this discrepancy record;
\ghissue{47} owns the Stage~4.3 decoder calculations, now discharged, and the
non-encoding support estimate.  No unrestricted theorem, residual assumption, or
additional witness field was introduced.

\section{Conclusion}

The decoding identity is false for a general polynomial outcome.  Restricting
it to the encoding image is a necessary local correction.  Recovering the
source's measurement-consistency conclusion then requires the separate
non-encoding-mass estimate, which remains an open proof obligation.

\section{Retirement criterion}

An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all three of the
following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item it is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
        outside result;
  \item no current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated;
  \item it assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data,
        repair data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper
        proof requires.
\end{enumerate}
If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, it
should remain a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.
It should not be a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should
not support a source-labelled blueprint \verb|\leanok| claim.

\section{Review questions}

A reviewer should first compare every paper-labelled declaration with the cited
source statement, checking both hypotheses and conclusion up to faithful formal
encoding.  Bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, and
proof-obligation assumptions should be absent from paper-facing theorem
signatures unless they occur in the paper.  If a conditional helper remains,
its name should be explicitly conditional and it should not support a source
theorem \verb|\leanok| claim.
Each load-bearing obligation-structure or input field should have a theorem
discharging it, a tracked issue, or an explicit \verb|sorry| at the obligation
site.  When a definition has changed, the downstream subtree should be checked
against the corrected definition rather than patched locally.  Finally, if the
formal statement genuinely differs from the source statement, a paper-gap note
should explain the mathematical difference and give a plan to remove or justify
it.

\section{Conclusion}

The project should prefer visible proof obligations over invisible statement
drift.  A tracked \verb|sorry| in the source-shaped theorem, or in the lowest
named internal obligation needed by its proof, is less misleading than a source
theorem whose assumptions have been strengthened.  Conditional helpers are not a
normal substitute for unfinished proofs; they are temporary quarantines for
substantial proof content, and they must remain conditional until the missing
obligation is discharged.  The paper-facing declaration is reserved for the
theorem proved by the paper, or for a documented corrected version whose
mathematical difference is explicit.

    24	## Pattern 1: Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations
    25	
    26	### The rule
    27	
    28	A declaration presented as the formalization of a paper theorem, lemma,
    29	proposition, or corollary must state the paper result, up to faithful formal
    30	encoding of the mathematical domain.  Its public hypotheses and conclusion are
    31	both part of the statement.  Adding a load-bearing bridge, residual, repair,
    32	obligation-structure input, hypotheses bundle, or assumptions bundle not present
    33	in the cited statement changes the theorem into a conditional helper.
    34	
    35	The project therefore distinguishes three objects.
    36	
    37	| Object | Public statement | Blueprint status |
    38	|--------|------------------|------------------|
    39	| Paper theorem | Matches the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/` | May be linked by source-labelled `\lean{}`; statement-level `\leanok` only when the statement matches |
    40	| Internal proof obligation | Proves a missing intermediate mathematical input from paper hypotheses | May contain a tracked `sorry` while the proof is open |
    41	| Conditional helper | Quarantines an unproved intermediate obligation | Not a paper theorem; no source-labelled `\leanok` |
    42	
    43	It is never allowed to change the public statement of a declaration presented
    44	as the formalization of a source-labelled paper theorem.  At the final assembly
    45	point, the paper theorem must either discharge the extra hypotheses internally,
    46	or remain as the paper-aligned statement with an unfinished proof while the
    47	conditional helper is given a different name.
    48	
    49	The preferred way to expose unfinished work is a named internal theorem or
    50	definition with a precise paper-origin docstring and, if necessary, a tracked
    51	`sorry`.  This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement
    52	of a source-labelled theorem.
    53	
    54	### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily
    55	
    56	| Temporary reason | Explanation |
    57	|------------------|-------------|
    58	| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |
    59	| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |
    60	| **Auditability** | An explicit temporary hypothesis is easier to find than an implicit assumption hidden in prose, provided it is named as proof debt. |
    61	
    62	These reasons do not justify strengthening a paper theorem.  They only explain
    63	why a short-lived helper declaration may exist while its remaining hypotheses
    64	are being actively removed.
    65	
    66	### How to proceed when a proof needs an extra input
    67	
    68	1. **Check the source statement.**  Read the corresponding TeX in
    69	   `references/ldt-paper/` before changing a theorem linked from the blueprint.
    70	2. **Keep the paper-facing declaration source-faithful.**  Boundary hypotheses
    71	   such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances, or
    72	   type-class assumptions may be faithful encodings when they are needed to
    73	   state the mathematics in Lean.  Proof data such as `BridgeInputs`,
    74	   `RepairInput`, `Residual`, `Package`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic
    75	   `Assumptions` is different: it is not a paper assumption unless the cited
    76	   statement says so.
    77	3. **Name the missing intermediate result.**  If the proof uses a mathematical
    78	   fact not yet formalized, state it as a separate proof obligation.  A
    79	   temporary `sorry` in this declaration is preferable to adding the obligation as
    80	   a hypothesis on the paper theorem.
    81	4. **Do not introduce conditional helpers by default.**  A helper whose name
    82	   ends in `_ofObligations` is a quarantine device, not a normal formalization
    83	   pattern.  It may remain temporarily only when it preserves substantial proof
    84	   content that cannot yet be connected to the paper hypotheses, has a tracked
    85	   discharge or deletion target, and has no source-labelled blueprint
    86	   `\leanok`.  If the helper would merely package missing work as an extra
    87	   hypothesis, restore the theorem with the paper statement and leave a tracked
    88	   `sorry` instead.
    89	5. **Audit the final statement.**  Every PR touching a source-labelled theorem
    90	   should compare paper assumptions and Lean assumptions, paper conclusion and
    91	   Lean conclusion, and report whether the Lean statement is exact, has only
    92	   faithful boundary hypotheses, or has extra assumptions.
    93	
    94	If a paper-facing declaration is temporarily proved by calling a conditional
    95	helper whose load-bearing input has not yet been produced from the paper
    96	hypotheses, the proof frontier must be marked explicitly.  The declaration
    97	should carry an `**Unfaithful:**` docstring section naming the non-paper
    98	dependency, citing the paper-gap note or tracking issue, and identifying the
    99	internal theorem that will remove the dependency.  A named proof obligation
   100	with a tracked `sorry` is preferred whenever possible, because it makes the
   101	missing mathematical assertion visible without adding it to the paper theorem
   102	statement.
   103	
   104	### Required metadata for new proof-obligation declarations
   105	
   106	A new declaration whose name contains a proof-debt token such as `Bridge`,
   107	`Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Producer`, `Input`, `Hypotheses`,
   108	`Assumptions`, `Obligation`, or `Witness` must explain its mathematical role in
   109	the def-site docstring.  A paper citation alone is not enough, because the
   110	reviewer must be able to tell whether the declaration is part of the paper
   111	statement or a Lean-only proof obligation.
   112	
   113	Use one of the following markers.
   114	
   115	| Marker | Use |
   116	|--------|-----|
   117	| `**Source:**`, `**Paper source:**`, or `**Source statement:**` | The declaration is a faithful formal encoding of a cited source statement or a field of that statement |
   118	| `**Faithful encoding:**` | The declaration records boundary data or domain data that the paper uses implicitly |
   119	| `**Proof obligation:**` or `**Internal proof obligation:**` | The declaration is a theorem or record that must be proved from the paper hypotheses before a source theorem is complete |
   120	| `**Conditional:**` | The declaration is a conditional helper; it must not be linked as the source theorem |
   121	| `**Unfaithful:**` | The declaration or proof currently depends on a load-bearing assumption not yet derived from the paper hypotheses |
   122	
   123	Proof-obligation, conditional, and unfaithful markers must cite a paper-gap note
   124	or tracking issue and must state the planned discharge or elimination theorem.
   125	If such a declaration would merely package missing work as an added hypothesis
   126	to a source theorem, do not introduce it; restore the source theorem statement
   127	and leave the missing proof as a tracked `sorry`.
   128	
   129	### Conditional helper boundary
   130	
   131	1. **Prefer a source theorem with a tracked `sorry`.**  If a proof requires a
   132	   construction that is not yet available from the paper hypotheses, the first
   133	   repair is to restore the source theorem statement and leave the missing proof
   134	   open.  Do not introduce a new `Input`, `Obligation`, `Residual`, `Repair`,
   135	   `Producer`, or `Package` merely to avoid that `sorry`.
   136	
   137	2. **Do not bundle several missing theorem-level steps into one hypothesis.**
   138	   The former Section 9 bundle `SelfImprovementObligations` and the helper
   139	   `selfImprovementFromObligations` were removed because they bundled
   140	   helper strong self-consistency, orthonormalization, and final-field transport
   141	   into a single route to the full self-improvement conclusion.  The correct
   142	   boundary is now the theorem `selfImprovement`, whose missing
   143	   proof is an explicit `sorry`.
   144	
   145	   The former induction-section helper
   146	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection_ofObligations` was removed because it
   147	   encouraged propagation of the Section 9 bundle into the Section 6 successor
   148	   constructors.  Those constructors now call the theorem
   149	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` directly; its current proof gap is the
   150	   correct place for the missing work.
   151	
   152	3. **Propagation is a warning sign.**  The consumer of
   153	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` — typically a
   154	   `MainInductionStep` theorem — should close the hypothesis with an internal
   155	   theorem as soon as possible.  If the hypothesis propagates upward toward a
   156	   paper-labelled theorem, the PR should stop and either prove the obligation or
   157	   restore the paper theorem with an explicit unfinished proof.
   158	
   159	4. **Final closure at the paper theorem.**  The theorem `mainFormal` in
   160	   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean` is reserved for the
   161	   paper-shaped statement.  If the witness needed by the final transport has
   162	   not yet been constructed from the paper hypotheses, the theorem should remain
   163	   an explicit unfinished proof.  Do not replace the missing construction by
   164	   extra bridge, residual, repair, package, or obligation hypotheses, and do not
   165	   proliferate named obligation declarations merely to avoid a direct `sorry`.
   166	
   167	   The paper-labelled `mainFormal` should have the hypotheses of the paper
   168	   theorem: a projective strategy passing the low individual degree test, the
   169	   stated parameter bounds, and the faithful formalization of the ambient
   170	   domains.  Bridge, residual, repair, and proof-obligation inputs must be
   171	   produced inside its proof rather than added to its statement.

   177	When such a declaration remains useful, its role should be made explicit and
   178	kept away from source-labelled blueprint entries.

### Existing bridge-like declarations

Several older declarations still name proof obligations explicitly.  They are
transitional proof debt, not a pattern to extend to paper theorem statements.
When such a declaration remains useful, its role should be made explicit and
kept away from source-labelled blueprint entries.

| Declaration | Status to maintain |
|-------------|--------------------|
| `LdPastingNontrivialContext` | Nontrivial-regime context for `ldPastingNontrivial`; do not present it as the unrestricted `thm:ld-pasting` context |
| `Pasting.ldPastingNontrivial` | Restricted nontrivial-regime form of `thm:ld-pasting`; link from a Lean-only remark, while `Pasting.ldPasting` remains the unrestricted source-facing theorem |

The former same-carrier `mainFormal` transport-witness route has been retired.
The former `SelfImprovement.HelperStrongSelfConsistencyInput`,
`SelfImprovement.OrthonormalizationInput`, `SelfImprovement.FinalFieldsInput`, and
`MakingMeasurementsProjective.OrthonormalizationInput` bundles have been removed.
Useful proof content should be kept as named construction lemmas, while missing
orthonormalization or final-field arguments remain direct proof gaps on the
source-facing theorem until proved from the paper hypotheses.

The former `MakingMeasurementsProjective.SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation
has likewise been retired.  The spectral-truncation step is represented by the
source-shaped statement `SpectralTruncationStatement` and by direct construction
theorems such as `spectralTruncationStatement_of_sourceAlmostProjective`,
rather than by an `Input` wrapper passed through later theorems.

### Retiring auxiliary declarations

An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all of the following
conditions hold.

1. It is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
   outside result.
2. No current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated.
3. It assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data, repair
   data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper proof requires.

If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, keep it
as a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.  It should
not remain a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should not be
the target of a source-labelled blueprint `\leanok`.

### Former proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean`

The former direct tracked proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean` and the
Section 6 successor route have been discharged under the corrected source
statements.  The theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` is the corrected
two-space source theorem.  The earlier same-carrier auxiliary interface has
been retired; the headline theorem carries no bridge, residual, repair,
package, producer, generic hypothesis, or proof-obligation input in its public
statement.

### Distinction from anti-patterns

This rule addresses the same risk as conclusion-shaped-hypothesis smuggling
(anti-pattern A1 in `docs/anti_patterns.md`), but it is stricter for
paper-labelled declarations:

- A conclusion-shaped hypothesis is always unacceptable.
- A genuine intermediate fact may appear only in a separately named conditional
  helper while its obligation discharger is being proved.
- That same intermediate fact is still unacceptable as an added hypothesis on
  the public statement of the paper theorem, unless it is a faithful encoding
  of a hypothesis present in the cited source.

Obligation structures that bundle still-unproved theorem-level steps are proof
debt under this pattern.  They should not be introduced merely because a proof
is blocked.  The preferred repair is to keep the paper-labelled statement
source-faithful and make the exact missing mathematical step visible as a named
lemma or as a `sorry` in the theorem with the paper statement.

## Pattern 2: Blueprint–Lean synchronization

### The three tags

The blueprint (under `blueprint/src/chapter/`) uses three LaTeX commands
to link to Lean:

| Tag | Meaning | Example |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `\lean{Name}` | The corresponding Lean declaration exists | `\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal}` |
| `\leanok` (statement-level) | The Lean declaration compiles and its statement matches the source or blueprint statement; it does not certify proof closure | `\leanok` |
| `\leanok` (proof-level) | The proof block is fully formalized — the theorem or lemma has a complete sorry-free proof | `\lean{...}` plus `\leanok` inside `\begin{proof}` |
| `\uses{label}` | The statement or proof block depends on the cited result | `\uses{thm:orthonormalization, prop:completing-to-measurement}` |
